articles.title: Choosing QuePaxa, an unusual consensus algorithm
articles.summary:
Choosing QuePaxa, an unusual consensus algorithm
Cloudflare recently announced Meerkat, an experimental distributed consensus service designed to manage our internal global control plane. It is powered by a new consensus algorithm published by researchers Tennage & Băsescu et al. called QuePaxa (2023).
QuePaxa is an unusual choice; most consensus systems use well-established consensus algorithms like Raft, (Multi-)Paxos or Viewstamped Replication. These algorithms are well understood, have mature implementations, and usually work well.
Unfortunately, common consensus algorithms often suffer in wide-area networks with volatile network connectivity and latency, i.e., networks like the Internet, which is where Meerkat runs. These algorithms rely on a single leader process being available and having predictable latency. If the leader goes down, experiences higher latency than usual, or is disconnected, the entire consensus system slows down or becomes unavailable until the leader is replaced. This is unacceptable for Meerkat.
Meerkat’s global deployment environment led us to a newer consensus algorithm, QuePaxa, which promises better stability despite volatility, in large part by not relying on a leader to make progress. In this post we’ll explain why we chose QuePaxa and how the QuePaxa algorithm works.

articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. articles.title: How AI Helps Recyclers Turn Mixed Waste Into Reusable Material
articles.summary:
As world leaders gather for COP31 in Türkiye, the event’s emphasis on zero waste puts a practical challenge in focus: how to keep products and materials in use for longer. Globally, less than 7% of the materials entering the economy come from recycled or reused sources. Municipal solid waste generation accounts for over 2 billion tons of trash per year — a figure that could nearly double by 2050.
AI and robotics are helping change this trajectory, as innovators around the globe improve sorting to recover resources that would otherwise end up in landfills.
“A more circular economy relies on making better use of what we already have,” said Josh Parker, head of sustainability at NVIDIA. “AI can help us understand what’s in a waste stream, identify what can be recovered and automate the work of sorting it. We’re giving innovators the computing tools to make those processes more effective and bring them to more places.”
See how four members of the NVIDIA Inception program for startups are applying AI to keep valuable materials in circulation.
Recycled plastic is only used if its cost and quality can compete with new material. Too often it can’t: Incoming waste is of inconsistent quality, sorting depends on hard-to-find manual labor and mixed scrap ends up downcycled into low-grade products.

articles.title: « Partout où on peut créer » : le CTO d'Adobe explique pourquoi il ouvre Photoshop et Premiere à Claude — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Depuis un an, Adobe ajoute de l’IA dans toute sa suite, mais il s’agissait jusqu’ici de ses propres assistants. À Adobe MAX, ce mardi 10 novembre, l’éditeur a présenté des intégrations MCP locales pour Creative Cloud, une fonction qui doit permettre à un agent IA extérieur de modifier directement les fichiers Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere et After Effects stockés sur l’ordinateur, comme nous l’expliquions lors de l’annonce.
Ely Greenfield, CTO d’Adobe et patron des produits créatifs, a expliqué le soir même, devant environ 25 médias réunis à Miami Beach dont Frandroid, pourquoi l’éditeur laisse des IA concurrentes piloter ses logiciels.
Un MCP dans la suite Adobe
La suite Creative Cloud va proposer un serveur MCP local. Pour les abonnés, cela veut dire donner des consignes à Photoshop depuis ChatGPT ou Claude.
Le MCP (Model Context Protocol) est un standard ouvert lancé par Anthropic en novembre 2024. Il sert de prise commune : un logiciel s’y branche une fois et devient utilisable par tous les assistants compatibles. Adobe peut donc s’y brancher sans favoriser un concurrent. Surtout, l’agent ne passe plus par un connecteur distant, comme ceux qu’Adobe proposait déjà dans ChatGPT ou Claude. Le connecteur fonctionne en local et travaille directement sur le fichier d’origine, dont les calques, les vecteurs et la timeline restent retouchables à la main.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert…

Le plus gros casse de l’histoire des cryptomonnaies est loin d’être terminé. Dix jours après le piratage de Binance, les pirates nord-coréens continuent de blanchir leur butin sur la blockchain. Selon le dernier rapport d’Elliptic, une société spécialisée dans l’analyse de la blockchain, les hackers fabriquent désormais leurs propres memecoins pour tenter d’échapper aux enquêteurs et aux forces de l’ordre. Souvent à l’effigie d’animaux ou de célébrités, ces cryptomonnaies reposent uniquement sur des blagues, à l’image du fameux Dogecoin.
« La plupart des gens voient les memecoins comme des jetons humoristiques dont le prix monte et descend au gré de l’engouement. Les blanchisseurs nord-coréens leur ont trouvé un tout autre usage : ils créent des jetons que personne d’autre ne veut acheter, et s’en servent pour dissimuler les mouvements de fonds volés », explique Tom Robinson, cofondateur et directeur scientifique d’Elliptic, dans le rapport.

articles.title: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
articles.summary:
Researchers at Google DeepMind have unveiled a new AI model designed to unravel how changes in our DNA affect different cells, giving scientists a more detailed view of a notoriously difficult problem that could hold important clues to the causes of disease — and point the way to new treatments.
Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
DeepMind’s new DNA model better predicts how mutations affect different cells, potentially opening paths to treatment.
AlphaGenome 2 is the successor to DeepMind’s genome-predicting AI model AlphaGenome, which was released last year. While nearly every cell in the human body carries the same DNA, different types of cells — from heart muscle cells and skin cells to immune cells fighting an infection — switch different genes on and off, and those patterns can change depending on what a cell is doing. As a result, the same genetic variant can have very different effects depending on the type and state of the cell.
The new model is designed to capture those differences, predicting the effects of genetic variants on individual cell types and states. Google said in a blog post published Wednesday that it offers a much finer-grained view than broader models like AlphaGenome, potentially revealing disease-relevant effects in specific cells that might otherwise go unnoticed.

articles.title: Mercedes lance une IA embarquée qui fonctionne même sans réseau : ce qui change pour les conducteurs
articles.summary:
Lancé en 2018 sur la Classe A, le MBUX de Mercedes est connu plutôt performant avec son interface réactive et son assistant vocal assez fin. Une bonne base que la marque allemande souhaite aujourd’hui améliorer avec un nouveau modèle d’intelligence artificielle développé en collaboration avec la start-up américaine Liquid AI. L’idée est de s’affranchir des derniers obstacles auxquels se heurtent encore ces systèmes.
Le principal problème étant le fonctionnement dans une zone souffrant d’une faible couverture réseau : généralement, l’assistant se bloque automatiquement en se limitant aux fonctions essentielles sans pouvoir poursuivre une discussion avec l’utilisateur. C’est frustrant, raison pour laquelle le système porté par Liquid AI pourra se passer de la connexion réseau du cloud pour continuer à travailler en bonne intelligence.
Confidentialité et réactivité : les deux grands atouts du système
Côté confidentialité, l’ensemble marque aussi des points car le traitement des données se faisant intégralement dans le véhicule limite les allers-retours vers un centre de données. Les informations sensibles pouvant éventuellement être échangées sont ainsi protégées au maximum. Aussi, ne pas dépendre du réseau permettra une latence réduite, ce qui améliorera encore l’expérience utilisateur.

articles.title: Threat Actors Exploit Openwave, Cisco BroadWorks Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Threat actors are exploiting two vulnerabilities in Openwave Webtop Media Transcoder and Cisco BroadWorks to access sensitive information.
Openwave Messaging provides email and messaging platforms, including webmail, to communication service providers. Webtop Media Transcoder handles document conversion, and Openwave’s advisory ties it to the company’s webmail.
The Webtop Media Transcoder bug, tracked as CVE-2026-111793, exists because administrator-defined file-type restrictions are not enforced, allowing users to convert unintended file types.
“This may allow an authenticated user to process and convert unintended document types if bypassing the webmail experience,” Openwave Messaging explains in an advisory.
Webtop Media Transcoder version 1.1.22.0, which rolled out in December 2021, contains patches. The security defect was disclosed on October 7, and a CVE record was published on October 16.
Japan JVN flagged the weakness as exploited on November 9, warning that an authenticated attacker could exploit it to upload a specially crafted file and obtain sensitive information.
The Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-20320, was disclosed on August 19 as an out-of-band blind XML external entity injection that could be exploited remotely, without authentication, to read sensitive configuration information.

Une entreprise peut y revendiquer sa présence dans ChatGPT puis, une fois vérifiée, mettre à jour ses informations clés et ajouter des flux de produits avec prix et disponibilités. L’idée est simple à comprendre : que ChatGPT cesse de recommander une référence en rupture de stock ou un tarif d’il y a deux ans.
Le Business Hub est ouvert à toute entreprise éligible située dans un pays où ChatGPT est disponible, d’après l’annonce d’OpenAI. Les marchands Shopify ont droit à une procédure simplifiée : ils peuvent connecter leur boutique directement, et leurs produits éligibles sont déjà intégrés à ChatGPT via le catalogue de Shopify. La tecnología permitiría, según Pontón, mantener videollamadas en las que los avatares reprodujeran el lenguaje corporal de los participantes en tiempo real, como si compartieran un mismo espacio virtual. articles.title: Microsoft corrige plus de 1 200 failles Windows, dont une brèche d'Outlook déjà exploitée par des pirates
articles.summary:
Réglé comme une horloge, Microsoft a déployé son traditionnel Patch Tuesday. Cette fois, l’éditeur corrige un total de 1 235 failles de sécurité. C’est un peu moins que le mois dernier. En octobre, Microsoft avait pulvérisé son propre record avec 1 411 failles corrigées en une seule mise à jour. Le rythme des correctifs déployés par Microsoft reste néanmoins hors norme.
Comme le mois dernier, cette avalanche de correctifs s’explique par l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle. articles.title: The Evolution of Commercial Open Source Software
articles.summary:
The Evolution of Commercial Open Source Software
Tony Wasserman | 11 November 2026
The Early Days
In the early days of computing, there were no software products. Some computer systems vendors provided mechanisms for their customers to freely distribute applications with their source code, typically through their user groups (e.g, IBM SHARE Library) [1]. Applications were custom-built, developed across many different computer systems using a wide variety of different languages.
The 1964 arrival and subsequent broad adoption of IBM’s System/360 and OS/360 made it feasible for developers to build software products that could be licensed to a large number of buyers. Soon thereafter, Martin Goetz was able to patent a software algorithm and to release Autoflow, the first commercial software product. Those steps led to today’s multi-billion dollar commercial software industry, with vendor-licensed products, accompanied by End User Software Agreements and patents.
Shareware
While vendors focused on enterprises and governments, the arrival of personal computers in the mid-1970s, created a consumer market for software products. In addition to vendor supported products such as Microsoft BASIC, other programs, collectively known as “shareware”, were developed by individuals, with their users asked to make a small donation (under $50 US) to the developer. Some of the most popular applications of this category were PC-Talk, PC-File, PC-Write, and WinRAR, all of which attracted many thousa…

Le système a été baptisé AlphaProof Code.
Pendant quatre semaines, des équipes comptant jusqu’à 80 agents d’IA ont travaillé sans interruption sur les machines de cinq chercheurs de Google DeepMind, avec une mission précise, démontrer mathématiquement que le code qui chiffre les conversations Signal tient ses promesses de sécurité.
Google a dévoilé le résultat le 10 novembre 2026. Le travail porte sur libsignal, la bibliothèque qui met en œuvre le protocole de chiffrement de bout en bout de Signal, dont des variantes équipent aussi WhatsApp, Messenger et Google Messages.
Prouver plutôt que tester
D’ordinaire, on évalue la sécurité d’un logiciel en le testant, en l’auditant ou en y cherchant des failles, ce qui permet d’affirmer qu’aucun problème n’a été trouvé, sans garantir qu’il n’en existe aucun.
Mais il existe une autre approche, la vérification formelle.
Reposant sur des méthodes mathématiques, elle consiste à démontrer, comme on le ferait pour un théorème, que le code ne peut pas enfreindre certaines propriétés. Problème, la méthode est réputée extrêmement coûteuse. La vérification de seL4, un noyau de système d’exploitation dont des chercheurs australiens ont démontré formellement le bon fonctionnement en 2009, a par exemple demandé l’équivalent de vingt ans de travail pour une seule personne.
Et c’est à cela que s’est attaqué Google DeepMind avec AlphaProof Code.

articles.summary:
As teams deploy and scale AI workloads using NVIDIA Dynamo, Kubeflow, or Slurm, tracking what actually runs requires visibility beyond the platform configuration captured in a recipe. Application teams define and update these workloads independently of the platform recipe, so a reproducible deployment bundle alone cannot establish which workload artifacts are running on each node. Mutable image tags like :latest add another layer of complexity. Two nodes can end up running different code under identical tags, and a node that pulls next week may retrieve an image that was not covered by an earlier security review.
NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR), an open source modular component of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, now includes a qualified AI bill of materials (AIBOM) component to close that gap. An open source project created by Google, k8s-aibom tracks AI workloads running on Kubernetes. Two stock recipes select k8s-aibom by default: h100-gke-cos-inference and h100-gke-cos-inference-dynamo. Other GKE recipes can opt in during generation with --runtime-inventory enabled. Recipes selecting it can opt out with --runtime-inventory disabled.
AICR turns known-good GPU platform configurations into version-locked recipes and reproducible deployment bundles. Each recipe records the desired configuration for one hardware, cloud, OS, and intent combination: its components, version pins, values, constraints, deployment ordering, and validation expectations. articles.title: CISA flags Cisco BroadWorks flaw as actively exploited in attacks
articles.summary:
The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned on Tuesday that hackers are now exploiting a high-severity Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability in attacks.
Cisco BroadWorks is a cloud unified communications (UC) software platform and the underlying engine allowing telecom carriers and managed service providers (MSPs) to provide branded cloud PBX, voice, and collaboration services to business customers.
Tracked as CVE-2026-20320, the security flaw stems from an improper restriction of XML External Entity (XXE) reference weakness in the Open Client Interface (OCI) XML Parser that can allow unauthenticated, remote attackers to read sensitive configuration information from vulnerable systems by sending maliciously crafted XML messages.
"This vulnerability exists because XML entries are improperly parsed due to external entity resolution being allowed by default. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted XML message to the Open Client Interface - Provisioning (OCI-P) service," Cisco explained when it patched the bug in August.
CISA flagged CVE-2026-20320 as actively exploited and added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday, ordering Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to secure their systems within two weeks, by November 24, as mandated by Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.

La herramienta puede ayudar a ordenar ideas, corregir redacción y detectar omisiones, pero no reemplaza el criterio de quien conoce su trayectoria laboral. Una hoja de vida debe superar filtros automáticos, aunque debe ser clara y creíble para el grupo de Recursos Humanos.
Kaspersky sugiere tratar a los chatbots como editores de texto y no como autores de una biografía profesional. Antes de cargar un documento, conviene aplicar pautas de privacidad, revisar el formato y comprobar cada afirmación.
Qué información hay que eliminar antes de usar un chatbot
Antes de compartir el archivo con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial, es necesario borrar el nombre completo, teléfono, correo, domicilio, enlaces privados, nombres de empleadores y copias de documentos.
Además, se debe omitir datos protegidos por acuerdos de confidencialidad, como resultados internos, listas de clientes, procesos de negocio o proyectos que aún no son públicos.
La precaución responde a un riesgo concreto: los servicios pueden almacenar conversaciones, usarlas para entrenar modelos o sufrir fallos de seguridad. articles.title: Les radars militaires peuvent désactiver une partie de votre réseau Wi-Fi et vous ne pouvez rien faire
articles.summary:
Vous êtes chez vous, et le canal 5 GHz de votre réseau Wi-Fi se coupe d’un seul coup : tous vos appareils basculent alors sur le 2,4 GHz, parfois avec peine. Aucune explication, vous vous dites que c’est un bug ; peut-être que vous redémarrez votre box. En réalité, c’est peut-être à cause d’un radar militaire si ce canal s’est coupé.
Le canal 5 GHz de votre réseau Wi-Fi se coupe tout seul ? C’est peut-être normal
Effectivement, votre box Internet ou votre routeur Wi-Fi peut parfois abandonner brutalement le canal 5 GHz et tout faire basculer sur le 2,4 GHz. Si vous avez un écran dessus, ou un journal, il y aura peut-être un message affiché, indiquant simplement « radar ». Il ne s’agit généralement pas d’un bug, mais d’un mécanisme réglementaire, baptisé Dynamic Frequency Selection (DFS).
Il oblige le Wi-Fi à céder la place aux radars, y compris les radars militaires. En France, les bandes 5 GHz ne sont pas entièrement libres : une partie est partagée avec des services prioritaires, notamment des radars. C’est l’ANFR, l’Agence Nationale des Fréquences Radio, qui gère les bandes de fréquences dans le pays. Concernant les bandes 5 GHz, parmi les radars prioritaires il y a ceux dédiés à la météorologie, l’aéronautique, l’armée, ou pour les communications satellites. Donc lorsqu’un routeur Wi-Fi détecte un signal radar sur le canal qu’il utilise, il doit arrêter d’émettre sur ce canal et en choisir un autre, le plus souvent le 2,4 GHz, qu’on trouve sur tous les routeurs.

The differences and engineering considerations behind choosing and implementing UCIe connectivity for advanced multi-die designs.
								November 11th, 2026 - 
								By: Synopsys
								
							
UCIe provides a common standard for die-to-die connectivity, but connecting dies in a 2.5D package is fundamentally different from connecting them in a 3D design.
In 2.5D designs, UCIe links traverse package channels where insertion loss, crosstalk, and increasing data rates influence PHY and package design. In 3D designs, shorter vertical connections and fine-pitch bonding allow bandwidth to scale through connection density, reducing the need for high-speed serialization, equalization, and channel training.
This white paper examines those differences and the engineering considerations behind choosing and implementing UCIe connectivity for advanced multi-die designs.

articles.title: Developers have been hacking around MCP’s file-upload problem for two years. A fix is taking shape.
articles.summary:
Developers have been hacking around MCP’s file-upload problem for two years. A fix is taking shape.
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has played an instrumental part in connecting AI assistants to external tools and data since Anthropic launched the project some two years ago. Want to have a coding agent check the status of a bug? Give it access to your issue tracker through an MCP server. Or ask an assistant how many orders your company shipped last week? Connect it to a tool that can query your database.
Part of the Agentic AI Foundation since last December, MCP has a roadmap that reflects the demands of running the protocol in production. For instance, maintainers have been working to make servers easier to deploy without keeping track of individual client sessions, and to let companies manage access through their existing identity systems.
But a perennial problem developers have faced is how to pass a file from an AI app to an MCP tool. For example, say you attach a PDF to a chat and ask the assistant to save it to cloud storage — the assistant can call a tool to save the file, but developers still have to work out how to get the PDF from the chat app to the tool. That can mean issuing a temporary upload link, or perhaps sending the user to a separate upload page.
To address this gap, the folks at the MCP project have outlined a draft extension that gives clients and tools a common way to handle uploads and downloads.

It is important to note that Moniepoint operates largely in Nigeria, with a recent expansion into Kenya. OPay operates in Indonesia, Egypt, and Pakistan, but derives most of its scale from Nigeria. It generated 88.1% of its revenue from the country in 2025.

articles.summary:
Home >
                                                                    Low Power-High Performance >
                                                                Variable-Length Prompts on Chimera GPNPU                                                    
Low Power-High Performance
                        WHITEPAPERS
		
How a flexible binary can serve every length up to the capacity you set.
								November 11th, 2026 - 
								By: Quadric.io
								
							
If you are sizing a language model for an edge product, the prompts it will see span a wide range. A spoken command is a dozen tokens, a pasted document is several thousand, and the same device serves both. Somewhere in the software stack, a decision is made about the gap between the longest prompt you provisioned for and the prompt that actually arrives. That decision sets how many binaries you build and qualify. It also sets how much of every inference is spent computing padding.
Most compiled inference stacks do not make that decision at all. A graph compiled for 1024 tokens processes 1024 positions every time it runs. If you send it 50 tokens, it computes the other 974 as padding. To serve short prompts efficiently as well as long ones, you have to build a separate binary for each length range and qualify all of them. Quadric Chimera GPNPU does not work this way. It gives you one guarantee and one optimization.

articles.summary:
Patchday bei Microsoft: Dieses Outlook-Update solltest du schnell installieren
Nutzer sollten ihre Systeme zügig aktualisieren: Beim aktuellen Patchday hat Microsoft nach Angaben des Unternehmens eine Outlook-Lücke geschlossen, die Angreifer bereits aktiv ausnutzen. Wer Windows Update deaktiviert hat oder Patches aufschiebt, riskiert auch noch weitere Attacken auf verschiedene Microsoft-Produkte.
So funktioniert der Angriff auf Outlook
Die ausgenutzte Schwachstelle (CVE-2026-124194) stuft Microsoft in einer Warnmeldung mit dem Bedrohungsgrad „mittel“ ein – dennoch sollte man den Bug sehr ernst nehmen. Für eine Attacke verschicken Angreifer eine Mail mit einer präparierten Office-Datei. Öffnen Empfänger:innen die Nachricht, baut Outlook eine Verbindung zu einem Server der Angreifer auf – und zwar ohne die sonst übliche Warnung vor externen Inhalten.
Dabei greifen die Angreifer Anmeldedaten in Form eines NTLMv2-Hashs ab. Mit diesem verschlüsselten Zugangsnachweis können sie sich im Namen des Opfers bei Outlook anmelden. articles.title: eBPF Rootkits: Why Underground Actors Are Taking Notice
articles.summary:
For years, eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) has been one of the most celebrated technologies in the Linux kernel. It lets developers run sandboxed programs inside the kernel without writing kernel modules, while powering everything from network monitoring to security tooling.
Linux is extremely popular in production servers and giants like Google, Cloudflare, and Meta rely on it daily.
The same eBPF capabilities that are attractive for defenders, however, can be a powerful weapon in the hands of attackers. Flare’s research found underground forum posts sharing eBPF rootkit code and step-by-step tutorials.
One Russian-language post described how to build an implant with process hiding and packet-triggered activation, and included screenshots the author presented as demonstrations.
What Makes eBPF Dangerous?
Traditional Linux rootkits typically rely on loadable kernel modules (LKMs) to hook system calls and hide malicious activity. These are well-understood by defenders, and most EDR solutions watch for suspicious module loads. eBPF, however, behaves in a different way.
An eBPF malware can hook into kernel functions, observe system calls, or inspect and modify network traffic using the same kernel-supported bpf() interface as legitimate tools like Cilium.
Its programs run without loading a kernel module, so a routine lsmod check can miss them. The challenge for defenders is determining who loaded the program and what it does.

The export policy for the category has been changed from 'Free' to 'Prohibited' with immediate effect.
The Indian Government has prohibited the export of lithium-ion battery black mass, a key intermediate material recovered during battery recycling, reversing its earlier policy that allowed shipments overseas.
In a notification dated November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, amended the export policy for waste and scrap of primary cells, primary batteries and electric accumulators. The export policy for the category has been changed from 'Free' to 'Prohibited' with immediate effect.
The new amendment covers waste and scrap of primary cells, primary batteries and electric accumulators, as well as spent primary cells, spent primary batteries and spent electric accumulators that are unsorted and do not contain lead, cadmium or mercury. The category includes lithium-ion battery black mass.
The amendment has been made under the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992, and the Foreign Trade Policy, 2023.
The move effectively bars exporters from shipping the specified category of battery waste and scrap overseas under the existing classification. It marks a shift from the earlier 'Free' export regime, under which such material could be exported, subject to applicable regulations.

AWS on Wednesday launched an emulator for AWS called AWS Emulator.
That, by itself, is interesting and may raise some questions about the future of LocalStack. But what’s maybe most interesting is that the emulator was entirely built by a team of agents and will also be maintained by them going forward.
Since AWS wasn’t sure it could actually copyright the work of these agents — and didn’t want to assert copyright where none may exist — the emulator is available under the Creative Commons Zero license, which puts the code into the public domain.
Tom ‘Spot’ Callaway, a principal open source software strategist at AWS, told The New Stack that there have obviously been other emulators in the past — and AWS itself has built some, too.
“The challenge is that they get out of date very quickly,” he explains. “They don’t always reflect reality on the ground, and because of that, they’re often not trusted. And we didn’t even trust them internally.”
With the rise of agentic coding tools, the team also saw a need for a better emulator that could help agents test code against AWS services without having to hand over AWS credentials to the agents.
Meanwhile, the team was also looking at a test case for building a full project with agents, and the emulator proved to be a good testing ground, in large part because it provided a bounded problem with clear goals and the ability to test the results.

articles.title: Managing performing assets when VC fund lifecycles expire
articles.summary:
Conversations about venture exits usually start with the portfolio company. Is the business ready? Is there a buyer? Yet as a fund ages, another question becomes equally critical: how long can the vehicle holding the company afford to wait?
The Stears–Ventures Platform Africa Venture Capital Exit & Liquidity Report tracks 181 verified VC-backed exits across Africa between 2011 and 2026. However, for a fund manager, the primary challenge rarely lies in underperforming investments. Instead, it stems from performing companies that retain meaningful upside but no longer align with the fund’s remaining life. This misalignment transforms an exit-timing issue into a residual portfolio paradox.
Market responses are beginning to emerge. For instance, GIZ’s ICAMA Initiative, alongside MEDA in Q3 2026, explores a Pan-African Secondary Fund for performing, de-risked late-stage assets. The core structural mismatch is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore: an investor may reach the end of a fund’s lifecycle before a company’s value can be realised on appropriate terms. This raises a fundamental question: what happens when the fund runs out of time before that value crystallises?
The three clocks

The infrastructure hosting AntiFox was used for various malicious activities, including vulnerability exploitation, webshell deployment, credential validation, configuration discovery, and AWS secret harvesting.
Initially created as a fork of ARTEX 0.1.1, AntiFox has a Chinese-language interface and lets users deploy AI agents and automate common penetration-testing tasks, such as mapping exposed services and probing target endpoints for vulnerabilities.
Security researchers at Arctic Wolf observed malicious AntiFox-linked infrastructure hosted on Alibaba Cloud using valid AWS identities, including IAM users and, in some cases, assumed EC2 roles, to make authenticated requests to Amazon Web Services APIs.
“In several recently observed intrusions, Alibaba Cloud systems hosting AntiFox interfaces were associated with confirmed malicious actions against internet-facing web services and associated AWS environments,” Arctic Wolf says.
One case highlighted in the report involved deploying an ASPX webshell on an internet-exposed IIS server, executing OS commands, accessing application settings and database connection strings, and copying configuration and log files to a web-accessible directory.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 built a shooter in 1 prompt — and it only took 8 hours and $550

Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 built a shooter in 1 prompt — and it only took 8 hours and $550
An Anthropic engineer gave Claude Fable 5.2 one prompt to build a first-person shooter and let it run for eight hours without human feedback. By the end, the model had processed 445 million input tokens, generated 2.7 million output tokens, and produced a playable browser game at an estimated API cost of $550.
The result was Saltline, a shooter set in a rain-soaked shipping port where players battle drones and robotic dogs while disabling communications relays. Anthropic engineer Felix Rieseberg shared the game when Fable 5.2 launched on Monday, describing it as an experiment in how much the model could accomplish from one instruction.
The engineer says Fable generated the game’s visuals procedurally rather than relying on imported assets. A public mirror packages the game into a roughly 1.4MB HTML file containing bundled Three.js code.
According to a note on the game’s title screen, Rieseberg spent about two hours improving the weapon models, sounds, and gameplay, while preserving a link to the original one-shot version.
The real price tag
YouTuber Matthew Berman took the experiment further, asking Fable to recreate a level from Gears of War: E-Day in Unreal Engine 5 using just three lines of instructions. The result was a playable shooter where players could take cover, fight enemies alongside AI teammates, and reload their weapons using the game’s signature active reload mechanic.

articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Introducing usage-based pricing for Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming
Usage-based metering for bidirectional streaming solves a software billing problem for real-time speech AI. Customers deploying streaming models on Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming pay for the endpoint infrastructure that hosts the model. Separately, model providers listing on AWS Marketplace need a way to charge for what customers consume during a live stream. Today, we’re announcing usage-based metering for Amazon SageMaker bidirectional (bidi) streaming inference, so model providers can report actual usage for the AWS Marketplace software charge. Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint infrastructure charges still apply.
Deepgram, the real-time speech AI company, is the launch partner for this capability, bringing usage-based Speech-to-Text (STT) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) billing to AWS Marketplace. This post builds on a series of innovations between Deepgram and AWS. First, we introduced bidirectional streaming for real-time inference on Amazon SageMaker AI, which supports long-lived bidirectional streams between clients and model servers. Then, Deepgram enhanced Amazon SageMaker AI support with AWS Identity and Access Management (AWS IAM) temporary delegation, simplifying secure authentication for enterprise deployments, and expanded observability with enhanced metrics. articles.title: Así funcionan estos procesadores que anticipan la llegada de un tifón y aumentan el tiempo de reacción
articles.summary:
AMD ha presentado la sexta generación de procesadores EPYC, una familia para centros de datos que busca reducir el tiempo necesario para realizar cálculos complejos en áreas como la ciencia, computación o incluso, en la predicción meteorológica.
Los modelos incluyen versiones con hasta 256 núcleos (las unidades internas que ejecutan instrucciones) y están orientados a tareas como inteligencia artificial, servicios en la nube, investigación científica y simulaciones técnicas.
Una de las aplicaciones mostradas por la empresa tecnológica está vinculada con el pronóstico del clima.
En una prueba con simulaciones de trayectorias de tifones en Taiwán, una configuración de 256 núcleos completó una previsión de tres días en 2,66 horas. La plataforma de referencia empleada en la comparación tardó 7,38 horas. Para una proyección de cinco días, el cálculo demoró 4,41 horas, frente a 12,28.
Estos tiempos pueden ampliar el margen para que meteorólogos y autoridades estudien una amenaza y definan respuestas ante fenómenos como tifones, lluvias intensas o vientos fuertes.
El procesador no anticipa el clima por sí mismo: ejecuta las operaciones matemáticas que requieren los programas especializados para elaborar una previsión.
Qué puede hacer un procesador en el pronóstico meteorológico

articles.title: Expensive accelerators, no workload-level visibility: Introducing Amazon CloudWatch accelerated compute insights
articles.summary:
Expensive accelerators, no workload-level visibility: Introducing Amazon CloudWatch accelerated compute insights
Accelerator bills have become one of the largest lines in the infrastructure budget. GPUs have become the most expensive resource in modern computing, and yet most organizations operate them with little visibility. A single training cluster can run for days and cost millions of dollars. Most organizations pool these accelerators across teams on shared clusters to keep them busy. But in these shared environments, platform teams cannot answer basic questions: which team is using which accelerators? Is the inference workload generating tokens efficiently? What is wasting money?
When a workload degrades (a failing accelerator, a thermally throttled node), teams find out only after a run crashes or the bill arrives. The device-level signals needed to find the cause (request traces, kernel logs, memory metrics from the accelerator itself) are not collected or connected. Without a way to isolate the problem to a single accelerator, teams fall back on cycling the entire instance, surrendering seven healthy GPUs to address a fault on one, and often waiting on scarce capacity to get the instance back.

articles.title: Microsoft promete hasta un 40% más de velocidad en los Windows 11 con solo 8 GB de RAM
articles.summary:
Durante las últimas dos décadas, la receta de Microsoft para hacer que Windows tuviera un comportamiento más fluido era sencilla: instalar más memoria RAM. Sin embargo, cuando la memoria RAM se ha convertido en un bien tan escaso (y sobre todo, caro. Carísimo), a Microsoft no le ha quedado más remedio que hacer lo que tenían que haber hecho desde el principio: optimizar el uso de recursos de Windows.
Por eso, Microsoft ha admitido que les ha tocado arremangarse para resolverlo, haciendo que Windows sea capaz de funcionar de forma más fluida en equipos con 8 GB de RAM.
Más datos en RAM, menos visitas al disco. Pavan Davuluri, jefe de Windows y dispositivos de Microsoft, publicó las cifras de esa mejora. Habla de una mayor capacidad de respuesta y de una multitarea hasta un 40% más rápida en equipos de 8 GB. Las cifras de la mejora suenan muy bien, pero antes de celebrarlas, toca ver cómo se midieron.
El cambio de mayor peso es una compresión de memoria ajustada para 8 GB. Según indicaba el responsable de dispositivos de Microsoft, Windows puede conservar hasta 2 GB más de datos activos en la memoria RAM, mientras que antes se apoyaba en la memoria de almacenamiento. Así, una pestaña o una app que dejaste abierta en segundo plano implica una carga menor para el sistema cuando vuelves a ella.

articles.title: Más de 30 años: un programador muestra el programa más antiguo que todavía funciona en Windows 11
articles.summary:
Si alguna vez te has preguntado hasta dónde llega la compatibilidad de Windows, un desarrollador que firma como Enlyth ha intentado responderlo buscando la aplicación con interfaz gráfica más antigua que todavía arranca en Windows 11 sin emulación ni modificaciones. El autor lo cuenta en su blog, donde apunta a que la búsqueda acabó a principios de los noventa, aunque con un poco de trampa puede llegar a retrasarse más atrás.
Sin sitio para los 16 bits. Windows 11 no puede ejecutar programas de 16 bits. Y es que, según la documentación de compatibilidad de Microsoft, las versiones x64 y ARM de Windows no admiten código x86 de 16 bits de ningún tipo, así que cualquier candidato tiene que ser una aplicación de 32 bits. Eso lleva a los inicios de Windows NT, cuya primera versión, Windows NT 3.1, salió el 27 de julio de 1993 como sistema de 32 bits.
Un solitario de 1993. Pero hay un atajo que adelanta un poco el reloj. Como explica en la misma entrada, en un foro anónimo alguien le habló de Win32s, unas bibliotecas que permitían ejecutar aplicaciones de 32 bits sobre Windows 3.1, o sea que hacían de puente entre las dos épocas. Las primeras versiones de Win32s traían el FreeCell, y la copia que encontró, del 22 de febrero de 1993, funciona en Windows 11 sin tocar nada.

articles.title: Broken: LearnArk’s mission to make tech truly accessible
articles.summary:
When Adedolapo Oguntayo-Williams arrived at a conference hosted by one of Nigeria’s premier banks in 2024, she was pushing her daughter in a stroller. There was no ramp. If a multi-billion-naira financial institution could overlook something as fundamental as a wheelchair pathway, what chance did persons with disabilities have inside Africa’s digital economy? She stopped waiting for corporate panels to figure it out. From childhood dreams of the cockpit and washing dishes in Cyprus on a state scholarship, to negotiating vendor contracts for Ruff ‘n’ Tumble and running global cybersecurity compliance remotely from Abule Egba, Lagos, Adedolapo’s career has never followed a straight line. Now, she is using that enterprise playbook to bootstrap LearnArk Inclusion Academy—a tuition-free tech training engine designed to move deaf, blind, and physically impaired talent from the margins into high-value tech roles. “Inclusion had to go beyond conversations and good intentions,” she tells TechCabal. “It had to translate into access, opportunities, and the ability for people to build independent lives.” In this edition of My Life in Tech, JOHN ADOYI charts Adedolapo Oguntayo-Williams’s journey from industrial engineering to building digital ramps for Africa’s most overlooked talent.

articles.title: Maersk confirms data breach as WhiteArmor ransomware demands $5 million
articles.summary:
Shipping giant Maersk has confirmed that a threat actor breached systems belonging to a company it previously acquired and stole data.
Ransomware group WhiteArmor claimed the attack over the weekend, threatening that it would release about 100GB of information allegedly exfiltrated from the company's logistics and supply-chain platform.
Legacy system compromise
The investigation into the incident is ongoing, but the shipping firm says that current evidence indicates that "no sensitive data has been disclosed."
Maersk added that it does not expect disruptions to operations, and assures customers that they can continue booking and managing shipments through its systems as usual.
“The incident is isolated to a local system, and we have found no indication that there has been any impact on other Maersk systems or customer and partner systems that connect to Maersk through integrations such as APIs and EDI,” Maersk states.
A.P. Moller–Maersk is a Danish shipping and logistics group and one of the world’s largest container carriers by fleet capacity. The company operates ocean freighters, port terminals, warehouses, and air and land transport services across 130 countries.
It has 700 container ships, roughly 13.5% of the global fleet capacity, 60 terminals in 35 countries, and employs 100,000 people. Last year, Maersk reported $54 billion in revenue and $2.9 billion in net profit.

articles.title: Pourquoi le Brésil inflige 1,2 million d’euros d’amende à Meta après le duel Lula-Bolsonaro
articles.summary:
Le Tribunal supérieur électoral brésilien n’a trouvé aucune preuve d’une manipulation volontaire des algorithmes de Facebook et d’Instagram en faveur de Flavio Bolsonaro. Il sanctionne Meta pour ses retards et pour des réponses incomplètes, parfois rédigées dans une autre langue.
La justice brésilienne a condamné Meta à payer 7,5 millions de réais, soit environ 1,2 million d’euros. D'après ce que rapporte Le Monde, pendant la campagne présidentielle, l’équipe de Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva accusait la maison mère de Facebook, d’Instagram et de WhatsApp de réduire la portée de ses publications pour avantager son rival de droite, soutenu par Donald Trump. Lula a finalement battu Flavio Bolsonaro au second tour, le 25 octobre. Les sept juges du Tribunal supérieur électoral (TSE) n’ont pas retenu l’hypothèse d’une « action délibérée visant à fausser le scrutin », selon les mots du rapporteur, Marco Aurelio Bellizze. Ils reprochent à Meta d’avoir répondu en retard, et de façon incomplète, à leurs questions sur ses plateformes.
Meta AI refusait les images de campagne de Lula
Au Brésil, si vous demandiez à Meta AI, dans WhatsApp, une image portant l’inscription « Flávio 22 », le numéro de Flavio Bolsonaro sur les machines à voter, vous l’obteniez sans difficulté. Avec « Lula 13 », vous receviez seulement un message d’échec. L’équipe du président a présenté ces essais au TSE, avec d’autres griefs.

articles.title: United won’t let your AI agent book your flight
articles.summary:
United says it won’t let personal AI assistants book tickets on the airline, citing both privacy and regulatory concerns.
United won’t let your AI agent book your flight
AI agents can’t attest that you don’t have explosives in your bags.
The company says it hasn’t yet seen many people try to use AI agents to book their flights, The Wall Street Journal reports, in line with observations from other businesses like Doordash. But United is concerned that agents could expose customers’ information or make purchases they didn’t intend, and potentially skirt federal rules about the kind of information airlines need to share with customers — like having them attest that their bags don’t have explosives.
While agents can still show users United flights, they won’t be able to actually complete the transaction on their behalf. The decision, and others like it, could limit the potential usefulness of newer personal AI assistants like Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots. “To be honest, I don’t want to create another middleman,” United CEO Scott Kirby said at an event on Tuesday, according to the Journal.
Across sectors, businesses are grappling with whether to let AI agents transact on their sites, and United is not alone in blocking access for unauthorized agents. eBay appeared to block agents from browsing the site, and several major banks have also placed restrictions on them. articles.title: OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
OpenAI is bouncing back from the doldrums it experienced earlier this year. The company’s quarterly revenue crossed $10 billion for the first time, thanks to strong demand for its recent AI models, Bloomberg reported, citing anonymous sources.
If true, that would represent an almost 50% jump from the $6.7 billion in sales the company reportedly recorded in the second quarter. That would also mark a sizable increase in its revenue growth rate, which was previously said to be about 18% between the first and second quarters of the year.
OpenAI’s profitability picture also appears to have improved, with its adjusted operating margin narrowing from -150% in the second quarter to -109% in the third quarter, the report said.
OpenAI, one of the first to commercialize AI models, wasn’t exactly struggling to continue growing its top-line expansion — 18% growth on top of $5.7 billion in quarterly revenue is massive by any measure, especially compared to most software businesses.
But it was seeing those gains be trumped by its archrival Anthropic, which has taken the lead in capturing the enterprise market for AI models and recently reported Q3 revenue of $17 billion. articles.title: UAEF: A framework-agnostic system for closed-loop evaluation of AI agents | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
UAEF: A framework-agnostic system for closed-loop evaluation of AI agents
Teams building AI agents on AWS use a range of frameworks, including LangGraph, LangChain, Strands Agents, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Each framework records agent execution in its own way, so the structure of messages, tool calls, and handoffs between agents differs from one to the next. Evaluation tooling tends to follow the same boundaries: teams build metrics, scoring logic, and result storage against a single framework’s trace format, and they must rebuild them when they switch frameworks or run agents on more than one.
This coupling makes a basic development question harder to answer: did a change to the prompt, model, or tools improve the agent? Answering it requires consistent metrics across versions of an agent and a shared record of past results to compare against. Agent quality also spans several dimensions that a single accuracy score does not capture: tool calling, response quality, responsible AI, performance, multi-turn conversation, multi-agent coordination, and reasoning.
In this post, we introduce the Universal Agent Evaluation Framework (UAEF). Customers across 12 organizations in the telecom, healthcare, and financial services industries used UAEF to evaluate their AI agents with one consistent set of metrics and compare agent versions before release. The policy required mobile subscribers to link their phone lines to verified national identity numbers. articles.title: Hardware-Based Location Checks Target AI Chip Smuggling (Texas A&M)
articles.summary:
Researchers at Texas A&M University published “5G CATS: 5G-Based Cryptographic Authorization Against Trafficking of Semiconductor Devices.”
Abstract:
“Enforcing export controls on AI accelerators requires verifying where a chip operates after deployment. Round-trip time measurements can bound a chip’s distance from a trusted landmark, but any jitter in honest replies forces the verifier to loosen its timeout, giving an attacker slack to relay traffic over fiber from a restricted region. Prior approaches either cross the untrusted host stack or rely on noisy power-line channels that inflate this slack. We present 5G CATS, a location certification system that pairs a co-packaged 5G radio, cryptographic engine, and hardware interlock on the GPU package with 5G Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) base stations. Terminating the radio link inside the package removes the host software, PCIe fabric, and baseboard management controller from the verification path. We map an authenticated challenge-response protocol onto 5G’s slot structure, replace permanent key erasure with short-lived execution leases, and specify a cross-check of the chip’s reported serving cell against the carrier’s own attachment records. In ns-3 and 5G-LENA simulations of an unloaded cell, our URLLC-based radio profile narrows the 99.9th percentile round-trip spread to 2.60 ms, more than ten times narrower than default 5G. articles.title: Citrix, Ivanti Patch Critical and High-Severity Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Citrix and Ivanti on Tuesday announced patches for 19 vulnerabilities in their products, including multiple critical- and high-severity flaws.
Ivanti fixed 13 vulnerabilities across five products, including two critical-severity defects in Cloud Services Application (CSA) and Endpoint Manager (EPM).
Tracked as CVE-2026-121683 (CVSS score of 9.4), the CSA flaw is described as a missing authentication issue that could allow remote, unauthenticated attackers to “add and delete arbitrary trusted EPM Core certificate entries”.
CSA version 5.0.8.1 patches the bug. Deployments running with a Dual NIC configuration cannot be exploited externally, Ivanti notes.
The critical EPM issue, tracked as CVE-2026-121653 (CVSS score of 9.8), is an SQL injection bug that could lead to remote code execution (RCE) without authentication.
It was resolved in EPM version 2024 SU8, which also addresses a medium-severity cleartext transmission of sensitive information exploitable via MitM attacks.
Ivanti released patches for four vulnerabilities in Sentry, including a high-severity remote code execution (RCE) flaw. Tracked as CVE-2026-105425, the bug was also fixed in Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM), along with five medium-severity issues.
On Tuesday, the company also addressed a medium-severity defect in User Workspace Manager (UWM). Ivanti says it has no evidence of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild.

articles.summary:
In a nutshell: The promise that personal AI agents would revolutionize the way we use ride-hailing apps, order food, and book accommodation is looking a bit shaky right now. Leaders of these industries say almost nobody is using the likes of Meta's Muse or OpenAI's Dots to interact with their services. Uber, for example, said only four rides were ordered through an AI agent during the week of Halloween, its busiest week in October.
Uber, DoorDash, and Airbnb have all said that AI agents are responsible for only hundreds of transactions on their platforms, a tiny fraction compared to the millions completed by real people daily.
Uber chief financial office Balaji Krishnamurthy said the company took around 320 million trips and orders across Uber and Uber Eats during the week of Halloween. In addition to just four rides being placed by AI agents, only 500 Uber Eats orders were placed by these AIs.
"It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far," said CEO Dara Khosrowshahi. "Listen, we hope that there will be more traction."
DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said it was a similar story at the food delivery company. He told analysts that AI agents have generated just several hundred orders in total since they became available. Muse launched on September 8, while Dots launched on September 29. DoorDash receives billions of orders globally each year.

Ukrainian drone operations squeezed by fiber optic cable shortage triggered by AI data center buildouts — Ukrainian defense firm reports 10X price hike as Russia secures 37 million miles of cable
The data center boom is negatively affecting Ukraine's war effort.
Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine sparked a new era of drone warfare. Russian invaders first used drones with fiber-optic tethers to combat electronic warfare on the front lines, but both sides now use these jam-proof drones. Against that backdrop, the AI data center buildout is making it harder for Ukraine to buy the fiber-optic spools that it needs to continue scaling its drone manufacturing capabilities. A research and development representative for BlueBird Tech, a Ukrainian defense firm specializing in drones, told Ars Technica in an interview that prices of fiber optic cables have risen around six to 10 times in the past couple of years as AI data center demand soaks up more and more of the supply of this resource.
According to that interview, It’s estimated that Ukraine and Russia are producing around 50,000 fiber optic drones monthly, with each drone capable of ranges of up to 62 miles. But Ukraine has only been able to acquire 72 miles of fiber optic cable from Chinese suppliers during August 2025, whereas Russia imported a whopping 328,000 miles during that same month. articles.title: Is Jensen Huang’s bad behavior more commonplace than it seems? | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The AI industry is still reeling from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s honeypot scandal, but some in the industry see it as an issue that’s much larger than one man.
The Chinese government has been active in economic espionage for decades, and with semiconductors at the center of the AI boom, there’s intense pressure to infiltrate any company involved. At the same time, many of the executives getting rich off that boom have made themselves easy targets.
As CEO of investment intel firm Heron Intelligence, Nate Singer has a unique view into the problem. His firm works on corporate due diligence: Essentially, making sure companies know the relevant dirt before making a major acquisition or executive hire. And while the Nvidia case is particularly severe, Singer says there are lots of similar cases in the semiconductor industry that have stayed under the radar.
“We’ve got former employees talking about behavior at senior executive levels,” Singer told TechCrunch, saying executives are “really crossing lines that should not be crossed.”
In a widely circulated LinkedIn post, Singer detailed one case in which a CEO’s wife made an unexpected board room appearance, “screaming about her husband and another company exec flying around in the corporate jet with a couple young ladies (who also turned out to be state-sponsored actors).”
It’s an alarming story, but an unfortunately common one. Singer says he’s seen at least three reports of similar cases, and suspects many more have gone unreported…

articles.title: Google's former CEO thinks AI has a marketing problem — but what if Americans understand the technology perfectly well and just don't like what it's doing?
articles.summary:
‘Our industry does a terrible job of marketing our benefits': Google's former CEO Eric Schmidt thinks AI has a PR problem — but maybe people understand it just fine
Ex-Google boss believes AI companies just need to up their marketing
Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt thinks AI struggles to convince Americans that it's a net good because of its messaging. After the U.S. election exposed growing public hostility toward AI, particularly the data centers necessary to power the technology, Schmidt argued in an Axios interview that the companies have done a poor job explaining the benefits of their products, but he is underestimating how much people already understand about AI.
"Our industry does a terrible job of marketing our benefits," Schmidt said. "We talk about all the negatives without talking the positives, and people are much more likely to index their minds on the negatives."

articles.title: Asus, Zoom Release Security Patches
articles.summary:
Asus and Zoom are among the tech companies that have released fresh security updates for their products this week.
Computer maker Asus published an advisory describing four high- and medium-severity vulnerabilities in certain router firmware releases.
Successful exploitation of the flaws could allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges or overwrite memory and cause a crash.
Zoom has patched two vulnerabilities in Workplace for Windows, including a critical-severity unauthenticated privilege escalation bug tracked as CVE-2026-108186 (CVSS score of 9.6).
The second issue (CVE-2026-108187, CVSS score of 8.1) could also allow remote, unauthenticated attackers to elevate their privileges.
Zoom Workplace for Windows versions 7.1.8 and later contain patches for both bugs. Zoom makes no mention of any of these flaws being exploited in the wild.
Additionally, Cisco updated several advisories: it added fresh information on Node2Shell’s impact and on an authorization bypass’s impact on ISE and ISE-PIC, and added new details on the availability of fixes for seven critical- and high-severity CVEs in Meraki products.
On Tuesday, both Cisco and SonicWall announced they have removed root certificates affected by compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates.
The fresh security updates arrived among hundreds of patches from Apple, Fortinet, Citrix, Ivanti, Intel, AMD, Microsoft, Adobe, SAP, and multiple ICS vendors.

Ring now wants its cameras to go and check on those spots themselves. The Amazon-owned company has unveiled an AI-powered indoor drone for homes and a rolling patrol robot for businesses.
The Ring Drone Cam costs $249.99 and is set to arrive in the US on January 27. It's essentially a second run at the Always Home Cam. Ring showed that one off back in 2020 at the same price, but it never actually shipped.

articles.title: Angular's TypeScript 7-Powered Compiler Enters Beta with Rust-Based Preprocessor
articles.summary:
The Angular team has shared details of a new version of its compiler, the Angular Preprocessor (ngp), which rewrites the analysis stage of the toolchain in Rust to clear the way for TypeScript 7 adoption. Alex Rickabaugh and Mark Techson announced the work on the Angular team blog in late September, shortly after Microsoft shipped TypeScript 7.0, whose Go-based rewrite removed the ts.Transformer API that Angular's ahead-of-time compiler depends on.
The existing compiler, ngc, wraps tsc and uses the Transformer API to turn decorators such as @Component and @Pipe into runtime instructions. The Go port offers no cross-language equivalent, and crossing the JS/Go boundary at every file would be prohibitive. The Angular team's answer is to decouple compilation from TypeScript's APIs and rebuild it on Oxc, the VoidZero Rust toolchain already powering Vite. The team pointed to the plan on X, framing it as a partial rewrite rather than a fresh start.
ngp runs in three stages. A Rust frontend using Oxc analyses files in parallel to discover Angular declarations and resolve metadata. The existing TypeScript template compiler then emits two artefacts, a runtime file containing the transformed component and a .ngtypecheck.ts file holding the Type Check Block (TCB) for template type-checking. Finally a downstream tool, whether tsgo, tsrs, esbuild or Rolldown, handles type-checking and JavaScript emission independently.

articles.title: Durante años nos hemos obsesionado con ganar músculo. Ahora la ciencia tiene claro qué es lo que de verdad importa para envejecer bien
articles.summary:
Durante mucho tiempo, la imagen de la salud muscular ha estado muy ligada al volumen que se tenía en diferentes partes del cuerpo. Y desde la cultura del fitness hasta las recomendaciones médicas más tradicionales, el mensaje parecía claro: para no envejecer de forma frágil, había que mantener la masa muscular. Sin embargo, este concepto va cambiando en los últimos años para darle mucho más peso a la fuerza que se puede ejercer.
El cambio de paradigma. El deterioro físico asociado a la edad se ha diagnosticado a través de la sarcopenia, un concepto que tradicionalmente ponía el foco en la pérdida de masa muscular y en la fragilidad. Sin embargo, el consenso europeo sobre la definición y el diagnóstico de la sarcopenia, actualizado en 2019 y liderado por investigadores españoles del Hospital Ramón y Cajal, cambió las reglas del juego.
El nuevo criterio establece la pérdida de fuerza como el rasgo principal e inicial del deterioro, relegando la cantidad y calidad de la masa a un segundo plano.
¿Por qué? La razón de este cambio se basa en un seguimiento hecho a casi 2.000 adultos mayores durante tres años, donde se pudo ver que la fuerza de nuestras piernas cae entre un 2,6% y un 4,1% al año. Es decir, perdemos fuerza hasta tres veces más rápido de lo que perdemos masa muscular. Y lo peor es que el mismo estudio demostró que ganar masa muscular no evitó que los participantes siguieran perdiendo fuerza.

articles.title: eMudhra revokes 8 more CA certificates after private key mishap
articles.summary:
Certificate authority eMudhra has revoked eight additional intermediate CA certificates after an investigation into its recent certificate security incident found improper handling of private keys during the certificate-generation process.
The new revocations bring the total number of affected intermediate CA certificates to 16, including eight previously compromised certificates whose private keys were so weak that anyone could recover them almost instantly.
In a new incident report published Tuesday, eMudhra said that both sets of certificates were affected by a custom Python script used to transfer private keys between hardware security modules (HSMs) in April 2025.
HSMs are devices designed to securely generate and store cryptographic keys, preventing sensitive private keys from being exposed outside the hardware.
eMudhra says it developed the script to move certificate authority keys between different HSM vendors at its facilities after delays in obtaining new hardware.
However, the script contained a bug that reduced eight ECDSA private keys to a single byte, making them extremely easy to recover.
The same script also processed eight RSA private keys, which handled sensitive key information in the memory of the computer running the script rather than keeping it protected within the HSM.
While the RSA keys were not weakened like the original eight certificates, eMudhra says it could not demonstrate that it handled them under its certificate security policies.

Harbor sert à télécharger et faire tourner des modèles open-weight (dont les poids sont publics, comme ceux de Mistral et beaucoup d’autres) directement sur un Mac équipé d’une puce Apple Silicon. Tout se fait dans l’app : on parcourt un catalogue, on télécharge, on charge le modèle. Les requêtes restent sur la machine, rien ne part dans le cloud.

Branchez deux Mac compatibles Thunderbolt 5 ou plus : Harbor les détecte automatiquement et additionne leur mémoire unifiée pour en faire une seule ressource de calcul. What to know about this year’s UN climate talks
Climate finance and fossil fuels top the formal agenda at COP31.
It’s that time of year again: Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists are gathered for the annual UN climate talks, taking place this time in Antalya, Turkey.
COP31 officially kicked off on November 8, marking the beginning of negotiations on one of the biggest stages of the climate world. Turkey and Australia are cohosting this year’s talks, which are scheduled to wrap up on November 20.

Die Forschungsergebnisse wurden kürzlich im Fachjournal npj Digital Medicine, das zum Nature Portfolio gehört, veröffentlicht. Künftig könnte das Werkzeug dabei helfen, Muster, die für bestimmte Krankheiten typisch sind, aufzuspüren.
KI-Modell zur Schlafanalyse
Bei Schlafanalysen wird die Gehirnaktivität meist per Elektroenzephalografie (EEG) aufgezeichnet. Für die Auswertung teilen Fachleute die Daten einer Nacht üblicherweise in 30-Sekunden-Abschnitte ein und ordnen jedem Abschnitt ein Schlafstadium zu. Das Ergebnis ist ein stufenförmiges Bild des Schlafverlaufs. Mit dem Modell AnySleep ist es laut den Forschenden nun möglich kürzere Intervalle abzubilden und entsprechend kürzeste Veränderungen der Gehirnaktivität im Schlaf festzustellen. Dafür verarbeitet das Modell die nächtlichen Messdaten und erstellt ein detailliertes Gesamtbild der verschiedenen Phasen des Nachtschlafes.

articles.title: Google DeepMind just mathematically verified key parts of Signal

Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself.
Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways. It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world’s communications on platforms like the Signal app, Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind’s formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code.
More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn’t have critical vulnerabilities.
Before the AI era, it was incredibly time-consuming for people to describe the characteristics of software they wanted to prove, turn these summaries into formulas, and then develop the proof. Agentic AI can significantly cut down the time of the latter project, enabling analyses like DeepMind’s Signal evaluation. articles.title: Critical Xen Orchestra Flaws Exploited in Attacks
articles.summary:
A threat actor has been exploiting a critical-severity authentication bypass and a zero-day in Xen Orchestra, software maker Vates warns.
A web-based backup, management, and disaster recovery solution for XCP-ng and XenServer virtualization environments, Xen Orchestra operates as an agentless control center across hosts, VMs, storage, and pools.
The critical flaw exists in the REST authentication mechanism, where an authentication token is turned into {} and then treated as an unfiltered lookup, leading to the first token being returned by token collection. If the token is not expired, the provider authenticates as its owner.
This opens a route that exposes reusable login token IDs, allowing unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication and gain administrator privileges.
“Xen Orchestra compromise can lead to arbitrary code execution on managed pools and a full XCP-ng node takeover as root,” Vates says.
The security defect impacts Xen Orchestra releases before 6.9.2 (stable) and 6.10.1 (latest), and Xen Orchestra Appliance, which contains Xen Orchestra.
Vates warned that the same threat actor has been exploiting this bug and a zero-day vulnerability that requires administrator privileges. The zero-day allows malicious VM imports that could compromise XCP-ng hosts, and a fix is still being developed.
According to the company, the attacker initially operated from 91.211.251.112:8001 and via the Tor network. No CVE identifier has been assigned to the security defects.

articles.title: The iOS Crash We Could Not Reproduce
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Intermittent production crashes often need controlled fault isolation when logs and local testing cannot identify the failing path.
- A lower overall crash rate does not prove that the root cause is fixed. Unrelated changes can simply change the timing of a concurrency defect.
- One device that reproduces a failure probabilistically can turn speculative debugging into testable engineering work.
- HTML import through NSAttributedString has a main-thread requirement that is easy to miss when the call sits inside asynchronous screen preparation.
- A shared main-actor abstraction is a stronger safeguard than asking every call site to remember a framework threading rule.
Some production crashes announce themselves with a clean stack trace. This one did not. It appeared in a large-scale consumer iOS application, affected only some executions, and resisted every local reproduction attempt. The final code change was small, but reaching it required turning a vague SIGBUS report into a controlled set of experiments. This article walks through the investigation and the threading contract behind HTML import in NSAttributedString.
The Crash That Refused to Reproduce
Most production crashes I investigate start with a familiar routine. I read the crash report, look for the stack frame closest to the failure, try to reproduce the path, and then work backward toward the root cause. This incident did not fit that pattern.

articles.title: Isabel Ocaña, administradora de fincas: “Un propietario no debe conectar el vehículo a un enchufe comunitario por iniciativa propia”

Así se pronuncia Isabel Ocaña, administradora de fincas y vicepresidenta primera del Colegio Profesional de Administradores de Fincas de Madrid. Se trata de la situación en la que se quiere utilizar el tomacorriente de la comunidad (por ejemplo, en el garaje) para la recarga de un vehículo eléctrico. En este caso, los dueños de los vehículos no pueden enchufar por su cuenta a los tomacorrientes de la comunidad.
El asunto tiene que ver con nuestro bolsillo. Si utilizamos el suministro comunitario para la recarga, los consumos se contabilizan en la comunidad. Recordemos que la toma de corriente y el suministro son servicios comunes.
En este caso hay que contar con el acuerdo de la comunidad y establecer un sistema de individualización de consumos. Es decir, que la comunidad disponga de un sistema que permita cuantificar el consumo de cada uno de los usuarios y que su coste se le cobre. Si se instala un punto privado en una plaza individual, los costes de instalación y de consumo de electricidad corren por completo a cargo de los interesados (artículo 17.5 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal).
En estos casos no es necesario un acuerdo de la junta. Es suficiente con informar a la comunidad de antemano. Hay que destacar que esto es aplicable a los puntos de recarga privados en plaza individual.
Por otra parte, la instalación ha de cumplir con el Reglamento electrotécnico para baja tensión. …

articles.title: SA fintech startup Lumepay raises $6m pre-seed round - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
South African cross-border payments startup Lumepay has raised US$6 million in pre-seed funding, alongside US$10 million in capital float, as it builds institutional-grade payment infrastructure for African businesses.
Led by CEO Harry Huang, Lumepay provides cross-border payment solutions for SMEs, corporates and institutions. Its rail-agnostic platform combines traditional finance and stablecoins to enable fast, cost-effective and transparent B2B transfers within and across African jurisdictions.
The startup launched Lumetrade, its digital asset and stablecoin trading venue, in April, before rolling out its payments platform in June, and has now raised US$6 million in pre-seed funding. How DXC Technology built a multi-model AI substrate on Amazon Bedrock
This post is co-written with Nick Tamburro of DXC Technology.
When an AI agent can act on a production server at a bank or a hospital, access to a capable foundation model is only the starting point. Recent public incidents, in which autonomous agents took destructive actions their operators never intended, show that the real risk is rarely the model alone. It’s an agent holding more authority than its task requires, with nothing in the architecture to stop it. Avoiding that starts with a substrate that governs model access at the infrastructure level.
Amazon Bedrock provides that substrate. Through a single managed interface, it gives DXC OASIS access to multiple foundation models: Anthropic Claude, Amazon Nova, Meta Llama, and open-weight families. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails enforce content filtering, personally identifiable information (PII) redaction, and denied-topic policies uniformly across every model. AWS PrivateLink keeps inference traffic within the customer’s virtual private cloud (VPC), and serverless scaling avoids self-managed GPU infrastructure as a failure point. Because these are system-level controls rather than bolt-ons, they gave DXC Technology a governed foundation for what no model layer can deliver on its own: a trusted harness that orchestrates, governs, and audits AI agents across enterprise IT operations at scale.

articles.title: Automating AWS Agent Registry updates with push-based architecture | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Automating AWS Agent Registry updates with push-based architecture
Every time a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server published in the AWS Agent Registry, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, gains a new tool or updates its schema, the registry record must be updated too. Without automated push-based sync, consumers discover stale metadata. For organizations managing multiple MCP servers across accounts, such a sync keeps catalog records current within an existing governance workflow.
In most enterprise deployments, a catalog’s value depends on its freshness. If a developer deploys a new tool on Monday, but the registry record still reflects last week’s schema, consumers lose trust in the catalog. Stale metadata directly reduces registry reliability, leading teams to inadvertently build dependencies on inaccurate information.
When an engineer adds a tool to an MCP server but forgets to update the catalog:
- Consumers miss out on the new capability entirely.
- Applications might call the tool using an outdated schema, causing unexpected runtime behavior or silent workflow deviations.
Multiplied across teams, this lack of automation erodes trust in the registry. Organizations ultimately fall back on ad hoc discovery mechanisms like hardcoded endpoints, informal knowledge sharing, and stale documentation.
In this post, we outline an event-driven architecture that automates these updates using AWS CloudTrail, Amazon EventBridge, and AWS Lambda.

The idea that Americans should be offered a greater choice of smaller cars has support from strange bedfellows indeed. After all, who could forget President Trump—usually one to take a maximalist approach to any problem—announcing last year that he wanted the Department of Transportation to make Japan’s diminutive “Kei” cars legal here in the US.
