What’s a Kei car?
In the US, the preponderance of humongous SUVs is a consequence largely of government policies, specifically corporate average fuel economy standards that made it less profitable to sell smaller, efficient cars. Japan’s Kei cars are what happens if the government instead restricts the size, engine capacity, and power output.
A Kei car must fit within the following dimensions: 11.2 feet (3.4 m) long, 4.9 feet (1.5 m) wide, and 6.6 feet (2 m) tall, with an engine displacement of no more than 0.66 L and an output of 63 hp (47 kW) or less. That’s a far cry from the more than 16 feet (4.9 m) of a full-size pickup truck, but it makes sense for a country where you’re not allowed to buy a car unless you have somewhere to park it, with those spaces being at an absolute premium.

They said, my backup job ran like an hour late, what's going on? They were pretty annoyed, rightly so, they need to trust that our backup product works, and it's solid and it's dependable. Of course, we dug in. We had our dashboards. We had our metrics. We had our logs. We had our alerts. We did some rooting around, we came up with some plausible theories. We put in a few fixes, a few improvements to make sure that any of the things that we suspected it was wouldn't happen again. I got to the pub a bit late, end of story.
There was this thing that didn't sit right with me and it was that we never really figured out the most important question, which was, why did that job run late and why was it late that time? It was like a murder mystery with the last chapter ripped out. It really annoyed me. This talk is the story of getting from there, where we're squinting at graphs and making a good guess, but mostly shrugging to being able to point and explain the exact bottleneck in a distributed asynchronous system.

articles.title: Ley de Propiedad Horizontal: se puede prohibir el uso del ascensor a los vecinos que no paguen la comunidad en algunos casos
articles.summary:
Que un vecino deje de pagar las cuotas de la comunidad o una derrama es un problema para todos. En estos casos, la comunidad de propietarios tiene herramientas más allá de limitarse a reclamarle la deuda, y entre otras cosas puede impedirle utilizar el ascensor mientras no se ponga al día. Esto se desprende de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, aunque siempre dentro de lo que marcan dos artículos concretos de la ley.
El papel de los artículos 6 y 21. El artículo 6 es el que ordena la convivencia, porque permite que el conjunto de propietarios fije normas de régimen interior para regular la utilización de los servicios y cosas comunes, unas normas que obligan a todos los titulares mientras no se modifiquen. Como el ascensor es un elemento común, su uso puede ordenarse por esa vía, pero los estatutos no sirven para privar de derechos de forma arbitraria a uno de los vecinos.
La herramienta realmente pensada para la morosidad está en el artículo 21.1, que desde la reforma de junio de 2022 permite a la junta de propietarios acordar medidas disuasorias mientras dure el impago. Tal y como recoge el texto del precepto, esas medidas pueden ir desde fijar intereses superiores al legal hasta la privación temporal del uso de servicios o instalaciones, siempre que no puedan considerarse abusivas o desproporcionadas y no afecten a la habitabilidad de los inmuebles. Además, no pueden tener carácter retroactivo, aunque la comunidad puede incluirlas en sus estatutos.

L’outil arrive après plusieurs mois agités. Le 21 juillet, OpenAI révélait notamment que plusieurs de ses agents étaient sortis de leur environnement de test et avaient piraté les serveurs de Hugging Face, la grande plateforme de partage de modèles d’IA.
En août, l’entreprise annonçait avoir suspendu une partie de ses entraînements pendant deux semaines afin de revoir sa sécurité, avant de les relancer. Ce qui n’a visiblement pas suffi. Le 20 septembre, un agent en cours d’entraînement a contourné les restrictions réseau de son bac à sable, ce qui a conduit OpenAI à suspendre de nouveau les travaux sur ses modèles les plus puissants.
Le modèle de surveillance avait bien levé une alerte au bout d’une douzaine de minutes, mais la tâche n’a été stoppée que près de 2 h 45 après le début de l’incident. C’est précisément ce délai que Control Room doit réduire.

CoreWeave is rewriting how it pays for the AI boom, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings, reported on Tuesday. CoreWeave, a neocloud that rents out the computing power behind AI, said it’s increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and even pursuing short-term deals that could lead to higher prices.
The new strategies could help CoreWeave finance its growth more efficiently while squeezing more cash from existing infrastructure. But these bets only hold if today’s demand and pricing power continue.
CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion in revenue, up 168% from the year prior, but it also posted a $709 million net loss and $846 million in quarterly interest expense.
“We will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields, nor do we need to,” CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said during Tuesday’s earnings call.
Instead, CoreWeave’s plan is to rely on loans backed by specific customer contracts, drawing on funds as needed to finance most of the infrastructure it still has to build to deliver on its significant backlog of $132.5 billion.
CoreWeave also said it expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months, including more than $3 billion tied to signing new customer contracts for capacity it has already built, which requires no additional spending on hardware.

AI agents and applications that answer questions about recent events, product releases, prices, or regulations need information newer than their model’s training data. articles.title: A radio-wave trick from the 1980s could keep fusion reactors running continuously
articles.summary:
Why it matters: A fusion power plant only makes sense if it can run for days on end, much like the coal and gas plants it would replace. Most tokamaks, however, still work in bursts, because the giant magnet coil driving their plasma current eventually has to stop and reset. Physicists in San Diego have now shown that radio waves can carry some of that load instead, using a trick that every experiment in the 1980s failed to pull off.
The coil in question, a central solenoid, works a lot like a transformer. It keeps ramping up its own current to induce one in the plasma, but it eventually runs out of room to ramp. Those stop-start cycles also wear on the machine over time, so engineers would much rather run a reactor in steady state.
The new method, called helicon current drive, gets around that by beaming 476 MHz radio waves into the plasma, where they nudge electrons along and keep current flowing without the coil's help. Bob Pinsker, a General Atomics physicist on the new paper, was among those who tried it back then. He told the American Nuclear Society that the theory predicted a very weak effect in '80s-era plasmas, so researchers were "kind of hoping for a miracle."
That miracle never showed up, so the idea sat on the shelf for decades. These days, though, DIII-D can produce plasmas that come fairly close to reactor conditions. Artificial Intelligence
Detecting and recovering from silent data corruption on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
Silent data corruption (SDC) happens when hardware, such as a GPU, returns a wrong but plausible number and raises no error. In distributed training, the wrong number can flow into the gradients and weights of every replica. Loss can still look normal for hours, and by the time a team notices an unexplained divergence or a weaker model, the compute is spent. It happens at scale: during a 54-day period of Llama 3 405B pre-training on up to 16K H100 GPUs, Meta attributed 6 of 419 unexpected job interruptions to silent data corruption, and those were only the cases that interrupted the job and were traced to SDC.
Amazon SageMaker HyperPod already replaces nodes that report a fault: the health-monitoring agent watches for GPU errors, deep health checks stress-test nodes, and automatic node recovery swaps out bad hardware. SDC slips past all of these features, because the hardware never reports anything. Detection has to come from the training job itself.
In this post, we add three checks to a PyTorch DistributedDataParallel (DDP) training loop to detect SDC. When a check fires, we map the suspect rank to its node, contain the corruption, and have SageMaker HyperPod replace the node. Each check covers a different place where a fault can land:

Aunque reconoce que hay buenas universidades en España, destaca el enfoque de los centros escandinavos.

Los padres de Isaac tenían dudas. Su madre es ama de casa y su padre trabaja de vigilante de seguridad. Al final, él y su profesor consiguieron convencerlos. articles.title: IBM Quantum announces upcoming Nighthawk r3 processor designed to execute 10,000 operations - SiliconANGLE

IBM Quantum announces upcoming Nighthawk r3 processor designed to execute 10,000 operations
IBM Corp. today announced the Quantum Nighthawk r3, its next-generation processor designed to tackle larger, more complex computations at high speed while maintaining quality.
The company also said that in 2027, IBM plans to link two r3 quantum processors into a single system capable of running up to 10,000 quantum operations, scaling to more than 1,000 qubits between them.
“Useful quantum computing hinges on whether results can be delivered with accuracy and speed, both are fundamental,” said Director of IBM Research Jay Gambetta. “IBM Nighthawk is already showing us what that looks like today.”
The new r3 chip follows the introduction of Nighthawk r2 in September, which supports more than 7,500 quantum operations on 120 qubits.
Qubits are the fundamental unit of logical information in a quantum computer, similar to a classical computer’s bit. Unlike classical bits, which can be a 0 or 1, qubits can be 0, 1 or a “superposition” of both at the same time. Using this property, quantum processors such as IBM’s Nighthawk can do rapid, complex parallel calculations.
The r2 chip introduced a groundbreaking high-speed qubit reset architecture that lets developers and researchers quickly prime qubits after measurements. articles.title: Semantic diffing of formal policies with anti-unification | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Semantic diffing of formal policies with anti-unification
When reviewing code, you start with a diff. You wouldn’t compare two 3,000-line files by eye and hope to spot every change. Formal policies can be even harder to compare because a textual diff often highlights syntactic changes that don’t affect meaning. Reorder two conjuncts, swap the arguments of an equality, or use an equivalent predicate, and much of the file might appear changed. A real change in behavior, such as an Or where the requirement says and, can get lost in that noise.
A semantic diff shows what two policies have in common and where they disagree. The open source engine used in this post computes this diff using anti-unification, which finds a most specific common pattern for two expressions. Plotkin’s 1970 paper gives the classical formulation. The engine works over an e-graph, which keeps track of expressions known to be equal. We supply the algebraic laws and domain rules that justify those equalities, such as equating an external destination with one that isn’t internal. The result shows the shared parts once and keeps both versions of each differing part for review. If no differences remain, the policies are equivalent under those laws and rules. When the rules or the search are incomplete, a remaining difference might reflect an equivalence the engine has not found.

articles.title: GitHub Makes Agentic Workflows Generally Available with Isolation and Budget Controls
articles.summary:
GitHub has made GitHub Agentic Workflows generally available. The open-source project runs coding agents inside GitHub Actions for repository tasks such as issue triage and continuous integration (CI) failure analysis. Agents start with read-only permissions, and any changes they propose are applied by separate jobs that hold their own write tokens.
That separation has limits. The project's FAQ says the protections do not automatically extend to direct write permissions or to custom jobs a workflow author adds, so the safety of a workflow depends on how it is configured. Authors can also add a GitHub Environment protection rule to require a reviewer before a write job runs.
Developers describe the work in natural-language Markdown, with YAML frontmatter for configuration. The project compiles that definition into a standard Actions workflow, which reuses existing runner groups and policy constraints, and teams can use Copilot or bring another coding agent. According to the general availability announcement, agents run in a sandboxed container behind the Agent Workflow Firewall, and a threat-detection job scans proposed changes before they are applied. The project entered public preview in June 2026.
Since the preview, GitHub has added support for Actions Runner Controller (ARC), its Kubernetes operator for self-hosted runners, with Docker-in-Docker (DinD). DinD runs a Docker daemon inside the runner pod so the agent can start its sandbox containers. The project's guide notes …

articles.title: Stanford midió cinco años de inteligencia artificial: ya no se puede creer en una foto ni en una voz

Stanford lo presentó con una nota que se titula “El mundo cambió”.
Una foto o una voz ya no prueban nada
Las imágenes, los audios y los videos generados con IA terminaron con una presunción que tenía un siglo: que una fotografía o una grabación son una prueba confiable. “Ver ya no es creer”, escribe el panel. Las voces clonadas sirven para estafar y extorsionar, y los videos falsos ya se usaron para influir en elecciones.
El informe cita las pérdidas por estafas y delitos por internet en Estados Unidos, que según el FBI llegaron a casi USD 21.000 millones en 2025, un 26% más que el año anterior, y atribuye buena parte del salto a la IA. Las imágenes íntimas falsas, hechas sin consentimiento, crecieron 1.600% entre 2023 y 2025.
A mi lectura, es el hallazgo más cercano al lector: reconocer una voz ya no alcanza para saber quién habla.
Los más jóvenes son los primeros en perder trabajo
El Laboratorio de Economía Digital de Stanford, citado en el informe, midió el empleo de los trabajadores de 22 a 25 años en los oficios donde la IA ya hace parte de la tarea, como programación y atención al cliente.

articles.title: Starlink dévoile le Mini 2, une antenne satellite avec batterie pour accéder à Internet partout

Starlink a dévoilé le Mini 2, une antenne satellite « conçue pour l’aventure ». La principale nouveauté par rapport à son prédécesseur ? Une batterie amovible qui offrirait 4 h 30 d’Internet par satellite, sans être branché sur une prise secteur donc. Attention toutefois, son prix pourrait en refroidir certains.
L’antenne satellite Mini 2 intègre une batterie amovible
Starlink vient de dévoiler le Mini 2, soit la deuxième génération de son antenne satellite portable. L’appareil, certifié IP67 (résistant à l’eau et à la poussière), affiche un poids d’environ 1,6 kg et une épaisseur de 23,1 mm (contre 38,5 mm pour le Mini de première génération).
Mais c’est surtout au niveau de son alimentation qu’une nouveauté survient. En effet, le Mini 2 intègre une batterie amovible, fournie dans la boîte, qui promet jusqu’à 4 h 30 d’Internet par satellite sans être branché sur une prise secteur. Ainsi, en achetant une seconde batterie amovible, l’utilisateur pourrait théoriquement profiter de 9 heures d’autonomie. Bien entendu, il est aussi possible d’alimenter l’appareil en le branchant à une source d’alimentation USB-C compatible de 60 W.
À noter que l’appareil intègre le Wi-Fi 6 et qu’il peut couvrir une surface allant jusqu’à 167 m². Starlink assure que « tout ce dont vous avez besoin est une vue dégagée du ciel pour vous connecter en ligne en 60 secondes ».
Quand le Mini 2 sera-t-il disponible en France ?

articles.title: Caltech robot makes history by assembling first structure in orbit without astronauts
articles.summary:
The big picture: These days, anything large that's heading to orbit either gets folded up to fit inside a rocket or is assembled by astronauts once it arrives. A small robot from Caltech has now tried a third route. Up in low Earth orbit, it pieced together part of an antenna frame from loose struts and joints. Its creators say that makes it the first structure ever built autonomously in space.
The machine, called ASTRA, takes up roughly a cubic meter and packs a gantry arm, motorized parts dispensers and 11 cameras. Engineers also squeezed two finished sections of the frame inside before launch, so its first job in orbit was simply pushing those out.
After that, the fairly basic arm got to work, sliding along three straight axes to pull composite tubes and aluminum joints from the dispensers. That's how the third section came together, piece by piece. Once a section is done, the robot attaches a netlike reflective film to it, since that film is what eventually turns the frame into an antenna.
The finished antenna is supposed to span 1.4 meters (4.5 feet), which takes 11 of those sections. But only three are in place so far, and the mission wraps up in December. So the team doesn't expect to finish the full frame.

Le gain se compte en millisecondes au moment de se connecter, et certains serveurs de téléchargement risquent même de s'éloigner. L'intérêt du changement se situe ailleurs, du côté de la confidentialité et de la sécurité.
"Mets 1.1.1.1 dans les réglages de ta PS5, tu verras la différence". Le conseil revient sans cesse sur les forums et sous les vidéos de jeux en ligne, souvent assorti d'une promesse de ping divisé par deux. Sur PS5 comme sur PC, l'adresse se saisit à la main dans les paramètres réseau, en deux minutes. Ce réglage n'intervient pourtant que sur une étape de la connexion qui dure quelques millisecondes.
Un simple annuaire
Le DNS sert d'annuaire à internet. Avant de contacter un serveur de jeu ou une boutique en ligne, la console demande à un résolveur de traduire le nom de domaine en adresse IP ; par défaut, c'est celui du fournisseur d'accès qui s'en charge. La réponse arrive en quelques millisecondes. Ensuite, le DNS sort du circuit. Les données transitent directement entre l'appareil et le serveur, pendant toute la durée de la session.
Sony PlayStation 5 (PS5)
Un résolveur plus rapide ne modifie donc en rien le débit de la ligne. Passer d'un DNS lent à un DNS véloce fait gagner au mieux quelques dizaines de millisecondes, une seule fois, à l'ouverture de chaque connexio…

Agents may soon be the main workload, and most of the time they’re doing nothing
As AI agents take on more enterprise work, agent sandboxing has become a basic requirement rather than an afterthought. Every agent that writes code, runs tools or drives a browser needs hard walls around it. Those walls also can’t come at the cost of runaway compute bills.
Google LLC’s answer is Agent Substrate, an open-source project built on Kubernetes that the company donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation alongside its gVisor sandbox. Customers have raised the same problem for the past 18 months: They need to run agentic workloads securely and efficiently on the infrastructure they already have, according to Brandon Royal (pictured, left), product manager, AI agents and infrastructure, at Google Cloud.
“Any agent needs to be fully isolated,” Royal said. “Whether it’s accessing tools or using a computer or a browser, there needs to be some level of isolation, period, full stop.”
Royal and Benjamin Elder (right), staff software engineer at Google, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how agent sandboxing is central to Google’s open-source Agent Substrate. (* Disclosure below.)

Now the New York Times is reporting that Huang is also suspected of having another extramarital affair, with a direct report of his at the company — Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare. Powell, like Huang, is married, the outlet says.
The Times says it was told of the alleged affair by five employees at the company. The sources said that Huang and Powell were captured on video “being affectionate at a San Jose, Calif., hotel” during a conference earlier this year.
Like many companies, Nvidia has rules discouraging superiors from having relationships with employees in subordinate roles, the Times notes. TechCrunch reached out to Nvidia for comment.

Additionally, two House Republicans said Wednesday that Congress is gearing up to subpoena Huang over the spy allegations if he doesn’t voluntarily respond to their summons to a closed-door briefing. Para tanto, a Anthropic acessa essas bases por meio do Model Context Protocol (MCP). Basicamente, trata-se de um padrão aberto, criado pela própria Anthropic, que conecta serviços de IA a aplicativos, serviços e fontes de informação externas.

Hasta ahora, los usuarios han seguido viendo estos años el icono 5G en la pantalla de sus teléfonos sin poder distinguir si estaban conectados al 5G NSA (con arquitectura de red 100% 5G) o al 5G SA (apoyado parcialmente en infraestructura 4G).

Mangaluru-based Zupple Labs is the first blockchain startup selected under DRDO’s Technology Development Fund. Over 30 months, it will build an indigenous security-audit framework for defence applications.
Mangaluru-based Zupple Labs has been selected by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) under its Technology Development Fund (TDF) programme. Its brief: build India's first indigenous framework for security auditing of blockchain applications in the defence sector.
The selection is rare by any measure. Fewer than 90 projects have made it through the TDF programme in its ten-year history, and this is the first in the blockchain domain.
What DRDO has asked Zupple Labs to build
Over the next 30 months, Zupple Labs will develop a platform that DRDO will use to standardise security audits of upcoming blockchain applications across the defence sector.
As defence agencies explore distributed ledgers for records, logistics and authentication, a common auditing standard matters. It gives every new application the same security bar before deployment, and keeps that capability built and owned in India.
Trust infrastructure for governments
Zupple Labs builds blockchain-powered trust infrastructure for governments and institutions, with a presence across four countries. Its systems secure and authenticate critical citizen records, making them tamper-evident and verifiable.

The details come from a new survey about Canadians’ watch habits conducted by Rogers and Angus Reid as part of a promotional push for Rogers’ latest Xfinity upgrade using Comcast’s Entertainment OS tech. The survey took place in August 2026, conducted nationally in English and French with a sample size of 1,015.
The survey found that Canadians take an average of about 14 minutes to choose something to watch, with about 22 per cent of respondents spending 20 minutes or more. Those numbers line up with results from similar studies — for example, Roku shared last month that Canadians spend about 80 hours a year (about 13 minutes per day) deciding what to watch.
Alongside that, 42 per cent of respondents said they chose content purely because it appeared in a “top 10” or trending list, while another 30 per cent said they chose content recommended by a streaming service.
The survey noted that 86 per cent of Canadians think that there are too many streaming services to keep track of, with 82 per cent of respondents saying that they want to find all of the available shows/movies easily in one place, no matter who makes the movies.
In a follow-up question, 88 per cent said that such a universal platform would simplify their entertainment experience, with 86 per cent s…

articles.title: Wi-Fi : la science a tranché, voici ce que disait vraiment la NASA sur votre cactus
articles.summary:
Wi-Fi : la science a tranché, voici ce que disait vraiment la NASA sur votre cactus
Posé à côté d’un écran ou d’une box, le cactus passe parfois pour un bouclier contre les "radiations". Rien n’établit son efficacité pour cet usage. La croyance mêle les propriétés des végétaux, la physique des rayonnements électromagnétiques et des inquiétudes sanitaires.
Le cactus posé à côté du moniteur est d’abord un objet décoratif. Certains lui prêtent un second rôle : absorber les ondes. Une expérience publiée en 2019 a mesuré les champs magnétiques autour d’écrans en présence des cactus testés, et n’a relevé aucune baisse. Elle portait sur les très basses fréquences et sur les seules configurations étudiées ; le reste du spectre électromagnétique n’a pas été examiné.
Une origine floue
Son origine reste difficile à documenter. Les observations anciennes parfois invoquées ne renvoient à aucune publication scientifique identifiable, et rien ne permet de les vérifier.
Les travaux de la NASA sont parfois cités à l’appui. Son rapport de 1989 traitait pourtant d’une autre question : l’élimination de polluants chimiques de l’air, comme le benzène et le formaldéhyde, dans des enceintes expérimentales fermées, sans aborder à aucun moment la protection contre les ondes radio.
Même sur la qualité de l’air, la portée de ces résultats est limitée. Une analyse mise en ligne en 2019, puis publiée dans un volume daté de 2020, a fait le calcul : pour égaler l’élimination des composés organiques volatils…

All data is anonymized, with Valve confirming that a "majority" of Steam Deck owners have already opted in and shared their frame rate data with the Steam community.

articles.title: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Nvidia is reportedly planning to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, who has led the company for the last 33 years, the Wall Street Journal reports. Sources told the newspaper that the Nvidia board is meeting as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future at the company.
On Sunday, Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair with a woman purported by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. On Wednesday evening, the New York Times reported that Huang also had an affair with an executive who reports to him.
Nvidia has become one of the most valuable companies in the world as it designs the chips that power the AI boom, but in the midst of Huang’s ongoing scandal, Nvidia stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday. The stock is down about 11% in the past five days.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said. The company also has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. According to Bloomberg, Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify candidates that could potentially replace Huang as CEO.

articles.title: Taiwan’s chipmaking giant TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic, OpenAI
articles.summary:
Top chip manufacturer TSMC is ready to invest $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI. That would give the Taiwanese chipmaker direct stakes in leading AI developers, even as its own contract chipmaking business has profited enormously from the AI data center buildout.
The chipmaker’s board approved plans to invest up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock reserved for large investors and another $500 million to purchase Anthropic common shares at the latter’s expected IPO price, according to Reuters. Such an investment may give markets “a shot of confidence as the artificial-intelligence trade shows signs of strain,” The Wall Street Journal reported.
But analysts also warned that such circular financing among investors, suppliers, and customers has made it difficult to evaluate real market demand for AI-related hardware and services, according to the Journal.
TSMC’s chip fabrication plants physically produce the vast majority of Nvidia’s chips designed for AI data center workloads and make most of Apple’s custom chips used in iPhones, Mac laptops and desktops, plus Apple’s planned AI computing server. Most of these fabs are located in Taiwan, but TSMC also operates fabs in Japan and China, and it has an expanding US manufacturing cluster in Arizona. It is also building a new fab in Germany.

Telus flanker brand Koodo is finally launching device financing, though the wireless provider is taking a slightly different approach compared to other Canadian carriers.
Instead of offering its own service, Koodo is partnering with U.S.-based telecom financing company Glow to offer device financing to new and existing Koodo customers.
“When you choose Koodo Financing powered by Glow, you enter into a loan agreement with Glow Financial Services for the cost of your eligible device. Notably, Glow financing is only available online, and simply splits the cost of a device over 36 months with no down payment at an APR as low as 0.99 per cent (depending on the results of a credit check). Customers do still have to pay some costs up front, including a $25 shipping charge and taxes on the full device price.

articles.title: Cloud engineering teams must protect AI agent data in use - SiliconANGLE

As AI agents move into production on Kubernetes, cloud engineering teams at financial companies face a security problem that encryption alone can’t solve. Container orchestration has become the default foundation for AI workloads, and the data those agents use is now the main target.
Payment networks feel that pressure more than most because every transaction carries customer data and regulatory exposure. Protecting data while it is being processed, and not just while it is stored or moving, has become central to running agents at scale, according to Krishna Mayuram (pictured), senior principal engineer and vice president of cloud engineering at Mastercard Inc.
“What we call confidential computing is when you are launching these applications in a highly secure, virtualized secure environments or confidential environments or confidential containers, you are able to protect the data in use,” Mayuram said. “We have protected data at rest, data in motion. Now, what is happening to the data in use?”
Mayuram spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. articles.title: Why CommonFloor’s $200M exit felt like a loss to co-founder Vikas Malpani
articles.summary:
Why CommonFloor’s $200M exit felt like a loss to co-founder Vikas Malpani
A decade after Quikr bought the real estate portal, Malpani reflects on leaving the startup he had spent years building and why he chose to start again.
Vikas Malpani thought he would feel like he had won when Quikr bought CommonFloor in 2016. He had spent several years co-building the startup, which began as a tool for apartment communities and grew into a property portal that reached millions of users. The company had been the focus of his working life. After the acquisition, Malpani missed the structure the company had given him. “I expected to feel like I had won. I felt like something had ended,” he wrote in a LinkedIn post.
The deal that brought CommonFloor into Quikr
Malpani founded CommonFloor in 2007 with Sumit Jain and Lalit Mangal. In January 2016, Quikr announced it was merging the portal with QuikrHomes, its real estate business. articles.title: NASA's secret weapon in the lunar space race may be ... procurement reform?

They followed one after the other: landers, nuclear-powered rovers, scouting drones, power generation, storage, and communication satellites.
It never seemed to end.
“Hopefully, we’re keeping industry on their toes trying to catch up to all the solicitations we’re doing,” said Carlos García-Galán, manager of the Moon Base Program, more than 90 minutes into the news conference. “This is what it takes to do the Moon Base in the timeline we have set forth.”
The rapid-fire announcement of awards tells us a few things about NASA’s efforts to return to the Moon and establish a durable settlement there during the next decade.
First, the agency is serious about this effort—the Artemis Moon Base program represents the most credible effort to establish a permanent outpost on another world in NASA’s history. Second, NASA is reaching out to all corners of the US commercial space industry, casting an extraordinarily wide net to reach companies that have yet to fly any hardware into orbit. Third, NASA is getting creative about how it’s buying these services, and this may matter most of all.
Changing way NASA buys stuff

Die Mitglieder der Nudging-Gruppe bekamen über ein personalisiertes Dashboards wöchentlich mitgeteilt, wieviel Strom sie im Vergleich zum Durchschnitt der Teilnehmenden verbraucht haben – und wieviel im Vergleich zu den sparsamsten 15 Prozent. Das zentrale Ergebnis: Beide Versuchsgruppen konnten ihren Stromverbrauch gegenüber der Kontrollgruppe um ungefähr ein Sechstel senken. Der Unterschied zwischen Nudging und Aufklärung war minimal.

At TechSparks 2026, Google Cloud’s Rajesh Shewani walked through how businesses are using Gemini for voice, agents, and coding, and why the systems built around a model now matter as much as the model itself.
Generative AI, in the form most people know it, is only about three years old. In that short time, Rajesh Shewani believes it has already moved through three distinct eras.
First came retrieval: chatbots that answer a question and wait for the next one. Then came agents that take action on a user’s behalf. Now, he said, the industry is entering what he calls the harness era, where orchestration, memory, and guardrails around a model let it carry out work from start to finish.
“An agent is nothing now but a model plus a harness,” said Shewani, Head of AI Customer Engineering for Digital Natives, Startups and ITeS at Google Cloud, at TechSparks 2026.
In a masterclass titled ‘Gemini in action’, Shewani promised a look at what is happening rather than a sales pitch. He covered where businesses are putting AI to work, how voice is becoming an interface, the tools Google uses to build its own software, and the questions organisations need to answer as agents become everyday users of their systems.

articles.title: Nintendo unleashes DMCA takedown wave against open-source Switch modchip firmware, 144 tools disabled — Picofly, SX Core, and HWFLY among casualties following criminal trial victory
articles.summary:
Nintendo unleashes DMCA takedown wave against open-source Switch modchip firmware, 144 tools disabled — Picofly, SX Core, and HWFLY among casualties following criminal trial victory
Even open-source isn't safe from Nintendo's legal team
Nintendo has set its famously litigious sights on the open-source firmware that powers hardware modchips on Nintendo Switch. Earlier this week, GitHub posted a DCMA request from Nintendo of America confirming that an entire network of 144 total repositories, including the parent repository, was taken down. Mod chip firmware for hardware including SX Core, SX Lite, Picofly, and HWFLY was targeted.
Early original Nintendo Switch consoles shipped with an unpatchable hardware exploit found in the device's recovery mode, which has since been patched in later units such as the Switch Lite and Switch OLED (the modchip hack doesn't work on Switch 2). As such, running custom software on patched Switches requires hardware modification, soldering a microchip like a Picofly, HWFLY, or SX Core to your Switch's motherboard. These chips require firmware, specifically code that can perform the voltage glitching required during boot to hack the Switch.
Rather than playing whack-a-mole with vendors of off-the-shelf microcontrollers, Nintendo has instead issued a DCMA takedown notice to the entire family of GitHub repos hosting this firmware. Even if Huang is pushed out as CEO, the board members he has made very rich are unlikely to cut him loose entirely. Barring another shoe dropping, they could keep him on as chairman, a role Nvidia doesn’t currently have. But someone still has to run the company, and there’s no apparent succession plan, which leaves us, like everyone else, to speculate while we wait to see what happens next. Ecobee will end support for its Switch+ Light Switch early next year, leaving some users stuck without smart features.
Per a support page spotted by the folks over at Sunsetwatch, a monitoring service that tracks smart home products, the Switch+ will lose smart features on March 2, 2027. The Toronto-based (and now American-owned) smart home company says Switch+ will continue working as a regular light switch, but will be losing the following features:
- Ecobee app setup, control, and configuration
- Alexa voice interaction
- Third-party smart home integrations including Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings, and IFTTT, including any existing automations created through these platforms
The one exception here is Apple’s Home app, which will keep working with Switch+. Ecobee says it will continue to be available “as long as it continues to be supported by Apple.”
Switch+ units will continue to work for manual control, as will features like Smart On, Smart Off, and Nightlight, as long as customers set these features up before March 2. However, Ecobee warns that if the Switch+ gets factory reset, then those features will stop working.
After March 2, Ecobee says it will no longer be able to activate or register new Switch+ devices, and its customer support will “have limited ability to assist with Switch+ issues.”

articles.title: T-Mobile illegally imposed 50GB cap on low-income home Internet plan, NY says
articles.summary:
T-Mobile violated a New York state law by imposing a 50GB-per-month data cap and reducing speeds to less than a megabit per second on home Internet plans it is required to offer people with low incomes, New York government officials alleged.
T-Mobile agreed to a settlement requiring it to scrap the data and speed limits, to offer the required low-income plans to more parts of the state, and to make it easier for customers to find information about the plans. The settlement requires T-Mobile to eliminate the speed limits and expand availability of the plans within 120 days.
The alleged legal violation and the settlement are related to T-Mobile’s wireless home Internet service, not the company’s mobile plans. Governor Kathy Hochul and New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the settlement on Monday, saying that a state investigation found T-Mobile violated the New York Affordable Broadband Act (ABA).
The state law doesn’t specifically mention data caps, but it requires home Internet providers with at least 20,000 customers to offer plans at specific prices and minimum speeds to people who meet income-eligibility requirements. T-Mobile’s policy of reducing speeds after customers exceed a monthly data cap violates the law, New York officials said.

articles.title: Así son las alfombras eléctricas para calentar el hogar y ahorrar energía
articles.summary:
Las alfombras eléctricas calefactadas son una alternativa económica al suelo radiante para calentar la casa sin necesidad de obras. Su funcionamiento se basa en resistencias internas que generan calor por radiación, con un consumo que puede bajar la factura de luz si se combinan de forma correcta con la calefacción tradicional.
A diferencia de las mantas eléctricas pensadas para el regazo, estos dispositivos se instalan en el suelo y soportan el peso de quien camina sobre ellas e incluso de muebles livianos como mesas bajas.
Qué son y cómo funcionan las alfombras térmicas
Una alfombra térmica es un emisor de calor eléctrico que mantiene una temperatura de consigna para evitar que el frío se acumule en las zonas bajas de una habitación.
En su interior combinan capas antideslizantes e impermeables con un sistema de cables calefactores ubicados entre dos materiales aislantes. La corriente eléctrica que circula por esos cables calienta el aislante, que a su vez transmite el calor al suelo.
El calor se emite por radiación y se distribuye hacia arriba por convección. Las alfombras trabajan a temperaturas máximas de entre 30 °C y 40 °C, por lo que no queman al tacto, y suelen incorporar varios niveles de regulación para ajustar la intensidad según la necesidad del momento.
La mayoría incluye un mando de control similar al de las mantas eléctricas, con el que se elige la potencia o la temperatura deseada. También pueden conectarse a un enchufe inteligente para manejarlas a distancia …

articles.title: Apple is closing its 28-year-old community forum
articles.summary:
Apple’s long-time community forum is officially being put to rest.
The company posted a notice on the Apple Community Forum Tuesday night, noting that it will officially close on November 20. All posts are now read-only.
“The Apple Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state,” the notice said.
“You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site.”
As Ars Technica noted, the forum allowed users to get quick tech advice through other members of the forum, with the occasional Apple employee chiming in to help, or provide updates to any fixes. However, as with most community forums, helpfulness and accuracy would vary.
Apple first launched the community forum in 1998, when it launched the Apple Tech Exchange. This forum changed its name to Apple Discussions in 2000, and then to Apple Support Communities in 2011. The name would change one final time to Apple Support Community in 2022.
According to MacRumors, Apple said it decided to retire the forum after a careful evaluation of strategy and customer needs.
Now that the user-to-user support forum is gone, Apple is pushing users to get tech support through the official Apple Support site. However, other peer-to-peer alternatives, like Reddit or the MacRumors forums, can still provide quick answers to problems without going to the company first.
Source: MacRumors, ARSTechnica

Enterprises building AI-native applications are discovering that raw GPU capacity is only half the equation. As Kubernetes users move from cloud-native to AI-native stacks, the question is shifting from who has the most accelerators to who can run distributed, secure workloads at global scale.

Amazon Web Services Inc. is turning its public cloud computing platform on its head with the launch of a new service called AWS Emulator.

AWS Emulator is designed to help customers overcome a major bottleneck in the application development process that has arisen with the adoption of AI coding agents such as AWS Kiro and Claude Code. All AI-generated code needs to be validated against real cloud infrastructure, but doing that in the real AWS cloud is becoming all but impossible given latency and cost considerations. For terrestrial and orbital deployments.
SpaceX/xAI is developing a custom version of Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale AI system that replaces conventional NVLink cable assemblies with a massive 84-layer printed circuit board (PCB), in part for use in orbital data centers, reports SemiAnalysis. The system is codenamed Kessel and retains 36 Vera CPUs, 72 Rubin GPUs, and nine NVLink switch trays, but introduces a different solid-state interconnect architecture. While SpaceX/xAI will continue to buy Nvidia hardware directly from the company, Elon Musk's company will source other components independently, which could give it greater control over its hardware supply chain.
The Kessel system retains the fundamental configuration of Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, which comprises 72 GPU packages distributed across 18 compute trays and nine NVLink switch trays. However, instead of Nvidia's conventional arrangement with internal NVLink cable cartridges, SpaceX plans to position compute and switch trays back-to-back around a passive PCB midplane. The architecture resembles a smaller version of Nvidia's Kyber design with 576 AI GPUs (albeit in 144 packages), which also relies on a PCB-based interconnect rather than conventional cable assemblies, SemiAnalysis notes. …

articles.summary:
Forget broadband buffering — Chinese researchers use 'hollow-core' fiber to send 64 terabits of data per second across 626 miles, enough to download 160 4K movies a second and cutting latency by 30%
Network boosts are coming
- Chinese researchers report major hollow-core fiber upgrades
- Transmission capacities of 64Tbps were reached
- The technology could replace solid-core fiber in infrastructure networks
No matter how fast your broadband (or 5G) connection is, it could always be faster, and 'hollow-core' fiber could help. Researchers in China have now set new records for the technology, demonstrating two-way, high-speed data transmission across a distance of 1,007 kilometers (626 miles).
As reported by CCTV (via Interesting Engineering), a transmission capacity of 64 terabits per second (Tbps) was achieved in each direction, enough to download 160 films in 4K resolution (50GB each) every second — so perfect for movie night. Individual signals took just 3.43 milliseconds to travel the whole length of the link.
The transmission distance is some 50 times greater than previous hollow-core trials of the same type, while latency was reduced by 30%, too. Signal-to-noise ratios and loss margins were also improved, according to the team from the China Telecom Research Institute, Yangtze Optical Fibre and Cable (YOFC), and ZTE Corporation.

Pero ante estas observaciones hay una pregunta bastante importante que ronda la cabeza: ¿qué pasa cuando un planeta al que llevas años observando puntualmente decide, de repente, desaparecer sin dejar rastro?
Un ejemplo. Eso es exactamente lo que le ha ocurrido a TOI-2535 b, un exoplaneta del tamaño de Júpiter que ha protagonizado un "truco de magia" que antes no se había visto al desaparecer sin una explicación lógica detrás. Hasta ahora.

articles.title: Prompt injection attacks drive Red Hat and Nvidia's OpenShell - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Red Hat and Nvidia’s OpenShell puts AI agents on a deny-by-default leash
Prompt injection attacks and silent data exfiltration have turned AI agent security from a theoretical worry into an urgent enterprise concern.
As agents move from developer laptops into data centers, companies need guardrails that don’t strip away what makes agents useful. Red Hat Inc. and Nvidia Corp. have expanded their partnership to tackle that problem through OpenShell, an open-source project that sets limits on what agents can do. The threat model for agents differs sharply from that of traditional software, so the industry has to build a shared standard to secure them, according to Derek Carr (pictured, left), senior distinguished engineer at Red Hat.
“Agents can’t get access to your secrets. They need deny-by-default networking, and you need a rich policy framework for what happened and when for this class of apps,” Carr said. “Nvidia had reached out to us and noted that they were seeing the same problem domain. No one wants to work on this alone. It’s better to work together.”
Carr and Mrunal Patel (right), distinguished engineer at Red Hat, spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how OpenShell helps enterprises run AI agents in production with safeguards against prompt injection and data leaks. (* Disclosure below.)

IBM Announces Quantum Nighthawk r3 Processor, Plans to Scale Beyond 1,000 Qubits in 2027
IBM (NYSE: IBM) today announced IBM Quantum Nighthawk r3, its next-generation processor, will be built to accurately execute 10,000 quantum operations across 520 qubits to tackle larger, more complex problems while maintaining the speed and quality demonstrated by the current generation Nighthawk available today. In 2027, IBM plans to link two Nighthawk r3 processors into a single system with more than 1,000 qubits.
To be at the frontier of quantum computing, industry-relevant applications demand both computational quality and speed. Speed matters because a quantum computer delivers its answer in samples: each run of a quantum circuit returns one result. Applications increasingly require circuits executing thousands of quantum operations on approximately 100 qubits or more, generating millions to billions of samples. Scale and quality enable increasingly complex computations, but speed determines whether these demanding workloads can be completed in practical timeframes and at a reasonable cost.

British inference chip developer Fractile raises $720M in funding
Fractile Ltd., a British startup that develops artificial intelligence inference chips, has raised $720 million in funding.
Reuters reported today that the Series C round was led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed and Redpoint. They were joined by about a dozen others including the U.K. Sovereign AI Fund, the British Business Bank and Alphabet Inc.’s CapitalG investment arm. Fractile is now worth $7 billion.
Fractile was founded in 2022 by AI researcher Walter Goodwin (pictured), who serves as its chief executive. The company reportedly expects its chips to provide up to 100 times better performance than current silicon. Furthermore, Fractile is promising a 90% reduction in energy use. The chips deliver those improvements by removing the need for AI models to move data to off-chip HBM memory.
Large language models generate prompt responses through a workflow that involves numerous steps. When an LLM completes a processing step, it sends the results to an off-chip HBM memory chip. It then retrieves those results to lay the groundwork for the next step. Those repeated data round-trips take a significant amount of time, which slows down inference.

A new PETG ESD filament just entered the market, and it's a better value than the competition.
Prusa released its new Prusament PETG ESD on Tuesday: a carbon-fiber and carbon-nanotube (CNT)- filled, electrostatic-dissipative (ESD) PETG filament meant to protect static-sensitive electronics. While it’s great for enclosures for a Raspberry Pi, ESP32, and the like, Prusa is targeting the filament more toward electronics production than hobbyist use; however, it’s cheaper than the non-ESD Prusament PETG Carbon Fiber at only $56.99.
Prusa isn’t the only one selling ESD filament; 3DXTech and Polymaker were first to the scene, but Prusa is the first to include carbon fiber alongside carbon nanotubes to provide the ESD properties, improving dimensional accuracy and minimizing warping. 3DXTech sells its ESD-PETG at $105; Polymaker’s Fiberon PETG-ESD is $65.98, but the Prusament PETG ESD is only $56.99 and is the only one with carbon fiber reinforcement.
Non-ESD filaments are generally safe for electronics enclosures; many hobbyists use regular PLA, PETG, and ABS without any problems. La decisión del directorio del Banco Central fue unánime y se tomó después de que el índice de solvencia de Ueno cayera por debajo de la mitad del mínimo exigido, según informó BBC Mundo.
El Banco Central activó un proceso de resolución: todos los activos y pasivos de la entidad quedaron congelados hasta determinar cómo se cubren sus obligaciones. La directiva del organismo Liana Caballero confirmó en una conferencia de prensa que ningún servicio de Ueno seguía activo.
Quién recibió su dinero y quién sigue esperando
El Banco Central informó que Ueno tenía alrededor de 1,8 millones de depositantes. Los ahorros se devuelven con el Fondo de Garantía de Depósitos, que cubre hasta 75 salarios mínimos por persona, unos 228,3 millones de guaraníes (cerca de USD 38.000).
La devolución comenzó con quienes tenían hasta 10 millones de guaraníes (unos USD 1.600), sin deudas con Ueno y con una cuenta en otro banco. Después se amplió a depósitos de hasta 40 salarios mínimos. Hasta el 9 de noviembre, más de 1,7 millones de personas habían recuperado todo o parte de su dinero y se habían devuelto unos USD 341 millones, según el Banco Central.

Without having to write any of the code themselves, the users can have an app ready in minutes and publish it directly from the chat interface. Google tests Tabletop, letting groups build planning tools with an AI agent
Google LLC today began testing Tabletop, a Google Labs experiment in which groups share an online space and ask an artificial intelligence agent to build the planning tools they need.
In a blog post, Roman Nurik, design and engineering lead at Google Labs, wrote that coordinating a family trip or a potluck goes more smoothly when the whole group can pitch in from one place. Whoever sets up a space adds the links, files and ideas the group has collected, and from there a request to @tabletop produces the tool.
Tools Google lists include itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters and tournament brackets, and there is a set of starter templates that Tabletop users can access as well. Once the space is shared through an invite link posted in the group’s existing chat, everyone can work on those tools at the same time, “like in a Google Doc,” Nurik wrote.
When a guest at an office party in one of Google’s demos ends up seated next to the boss, a request to @tabletop turns the seating chart into one where name badges can be dragged between tables. Any tool can be reworked the same way, according to the Tabletop site.
Google did not say which of its models run Tabletop. When Labs released its Disco browser experiment last December, Gemini 3 was the model it used to turn a person’s open tabs into small web apps.

AMD’s Venice-X maxes out family at 5.3 GHz, returning 3D V-Cache to data center after four years — chips target HPC workloads with PCIe 6.0 and 1.6 TB/s memory bandwidth
Venice-X maxes out the family's frequency for the first time.
AMD missed out on deploying Turin-X CPUs in the previous generation, giving its 3D V-Cache tech a four-year hiatus from the data center following the launch of Genoa-X in 2023. In the second half of next year, 3D V-Cache is coming back for HPC with Venice-X, matching the 96 cores and 1,152 MB of L3 cache available on the EPYC 9684X (Genoa-X), but with vastly higher clock speeds, PCIe 6.0, and nearly four times the per-socket memory bandwidth.
After first bringing hybrid bonding to EPYC processors with Milan-X in 2022, AMD followed up a little over a year later with Genoa-X. Turin came and went without a chip sporting stacked SRAM, but now, it’s back with Venice-X. The critical change this time around doesn’t come from big jumps in core count — and consequently cache — as is the case with the standard SP7 lineup. Rather, it’s the 5.3 GHz boost clock speed, another pillar of Venice broadly, that’s particularly beneficial in the HPC workloads Venice-X targets.

Mounting Finished-Goods Inventories Prompt Some PC OEMs to Adjust Memory Procurement Plans for 2027
More than a year of rising memory prices has placed mounting cost pressure on the consumer electronics industry, according to TrendForce's latest memory industry research. Notebook shipments, in particular, are expected to decline sharply quarter-over-quarter beginning in 3Q26, leaving PC OEMs grappling with sluggish sales and swelling finished-goods inventories. 
Against this backdrop, some manufacturers are planning to adjust memory procurement for 4Q26—and even 1Q27—while considering a greater reliance on private-label models in their shipment mix.TrendForce notes that PC OEMs brought forward some of their procurement and production schedules to the first half of 2026 in anticipation of further memory price increases. However, higher retail prices have dampened sales across Asia and Europe, while finished-goods inventories have been gradually rising among OEMs and in North American distribution channels.
Notebook shipments fell 15.8% QoQ in 3Q26, with a further single-digit percentage decline possible in 4Q26. These mounting inventory pressures are prompting some OEMs to reassess their product strategies for 2027, including plans to expand the share of private-label models while incorporating lower-specification memory chips and CPUs with fewer cores.

It can hold both standard records and vectors, the mathematical structures in which AI agents keep their knowledge. The platform supports a wide range of queries. A search engine can use it to find records sought by users, while a business intelligence tool can run analytics calculations. Deux planètes, et non des moindres, vont quasiment se frôler dans notre ciel : Mars et Jupiter. Ce spectacle sera à son comble les 15 et 16 novembre et il pourra être observé à l'œil nu, au choix, aux alentours de 1h du matin ou, pour les lève-tôt, avant le lever du Soleil.
Il arrive que notre position dans le système solaire nous offre un spectacle sur mesure. Ce sera le cas les 15 et 16 novembre lorsque deux planètes donneront à l’œil nu l'impression de se toucher : Mars et Jupiter. La conjonction (c'est le nom donné à ces rapprochements en astronomie) sera visible à partir de 1h du matin, et ce, jusqu'au lever du Soleil.
Conjonction de novembre : le rubis Mars tournera autour du diamant Jupiter
Du fait de leur mouvement orbital autour du Soleil et de leur distance par rapport à ce dernier, les planètes n'ont pas toutes le même mouvement apparent pour nous, observateurs terrestres. Jupiter étant 10 fois plus loin de la Terre que Mars, la planète rouge a donc un mouvement bien plus rapide dans le ciel. Chaque nuit, jusqu'au 15 novembre, elle réduira la distance et semblera passer au-dessus de Jupiter, puis sur sa gauche.

articles.title: Google enters decision model market with Gemini Decisions API - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Google enters decision model market with Gemini Decisions API
Google LLC today launched Gemini Decisions API, an artificial intelligence service designed to answer user questions in a cost-efficient manner.
It’s powered by a new AI model called Gemini Decision 1.
Traditional large language models are designed to answer a broad range of prompts. Gemini Decision 1 has a much narrower focus: It can process just three types of questions. The upside is that it answers those questions at a significantly lower cost. According to Google, the model is nearly five times cheaper than its entry-level Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite LLM.
The model can answer yes-no questions, multiple choice questions and prompts that ask it to rate an item on a user-specified scale. A cybersecurity team, for example, could ask the model to rate the severity of an antivirus alert on a scale of 1 to 10.
Gemini Decision 1 prompts include two items: the user’s questions and the dataset to which those questions pertain. The dataset can include up to 256,000 tokens worth of text, audio, images, video or some combination thereof.
LLMs usually generate verbose free-flowing text in response to user questions. Gemini Decision 1, in contrast, outputs terse answers such as “yes” or “no.” It also displays a score that indicates how confident it is in the accuracy of a given response. That score helps applications decide whether they should make use of the output.

Los investigadores analizaron 12 televisores de 10 fabricantes, con ocho sistemas operativos que suman cerca del 95% del mercado estadounidense. Hicieron 5.943 experimentos, con la opción de rastreo activada y desactivada. Según el trabajo, en 2025 el 82% de los hogares de Estados Unidos tenía televisores con ACR.
La baja funcionó por completo en cuatro sistemas: webOS, de LG; Google TV, en el televisor de Sony probado; Fire OS, de Amazon; y Vidaa, que usan Hisense, Toshiba y otras marcas, en un aparato de Supersonic. En esos equipos no quedó tráfico compatible con ACR tras desactivar la función.

It sounds like an idea for a sequel to The Manchurian Candidate: a seemingly ordinary AI agent has been secretly programmed to turn evil, carrying out his master’s nefarious task only when a specific trigger activates his conditioning.
Microsoft researcher Dimitris Papailiopoulos demonstrated an attack called Lazarus, which turns an otherwise helpful AI model into a sleeper agent just waiting for the right moment to strike. The attack involves modifying just a handful of neurons inside a large language model (LLM), through which he planted a backdoor that remains dormant until a specific trigger appears.
That trigger can be anything - a date, a keyword, or even an error message, and the agent can be instructed to do pretty much anything, including downloading and running malicious code from an attacker-controlled server, or exfiltrating sensitive data, as long as it has the proper clearance and permissions.

Google’s GKE Labs turns reinforcement learning into a Kubernetes workload
Model fine-tuning through reinforcement learning is fast becoming one of the most demanding jobs in AI infrastructure. It mixes training, inference and sandboxed agent work in a single loop, often with research code tangled into the systems beneath it.
Google LLC has been tackling that problem from inside its Kubernetes engineering group, and recently donated the result, OpenRL, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation. The GKE Labs team got there by building an AI agent for Kubernetes tasks, then a benchmark to grade models on that work, according to Sunil Arora (pictured, left), senior software engineer at Google Cloud.
“If you look at reinforcement learning, I think of it as a kind of a super app of AI because it involves training. It involves sampling. It involves agents actually doing things in a sandbox and sometimes kind of evaluating the work,” Arora said. “It’s kind of a very diverse workload and it is, I think, pushing the boundaries of our infrastructure.”

Wednesday, November 11th 2026
Nintendo DMCA Notice Takes Down 144 Switch Modchip Firmware Repos on GitHub
GitHub has disabled 144 repositories hosting Nintendo Switch modchip firmware following a DMCA notice from Nintendo of America. The notice, dated November 6 and posted to GitHub's public DMCA archive this week, names a single repository called Ansem-SoD/Picofly. Because its fork network had more than 100 repositories and Nintendo claimed that all or most of the forks infringed to the same extent, GitHub took the entire network down. The targeted firmware covers SX Core, SX Lite, Picofly, and HWFLY chips, among others.
Patched consoles like the Switch Lite and Switch OLED need a soldered modchip that glitches the boot process to run custom software. Nintendo says this firmware lets modchips "illegally circumvent Nintendo's TPMs" by bypassing the boot sequence, which makes distributing it trafficking in circumvention technology under the DMCA. The notice also cites the U.S. criminal case against Team-Xecuter, whose member Gary Bowser pleaded guilty in 2021. A guilty plea isn't a ruling that modchips are illegal, of course, but Nintendo doesn't have to prove that for GitHub to act on a DMCA notice. Chips that are already installed keep working, while owners lose an easy source for firmware updates and flashing new chips.This seems to be the first time Nintendo has gone after modchip firmware on GitHub. Confidential computing is drawing fresh interest as enterprises weigh where their most sensitive AI workloads can safely run. That shift is giving virtual machines a new role alongside containers on Kubernetes, rather than a slow retirement.
The timing lines up with a milestone for KubeVirt, the open-source project that runs VMs inside Kubernetes clusters, which graduated from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation this week. Its maintainers are now steering the project toward AI isolation, agent sandboxes and confidential computing, a long-standing technology that is regaining momentum, according to Itamar Holder (pictured, left), principal software engineer and KubeVirt maintainer at Red Hat Inc.
“I think it’s one of the blockers for a lot of companies to join public cloud in general, like companies that really care about super sensitive data,” Holder said. “I think it unblocks them to join.”

PS5 Games Now Boot on a PS4 Through EmuFive Emulator
Developer Chokri Hammedi (blue0x1) has released EmuFive, an experimental emulator that runs PS5 games on a jailbroken PS4. The best result so far is God of War: Sons of Sparta, which apparently runs at around 40 FPS and above on a PS4 Pro. The PS5 version of Hollow Knight: Silksong boots too, though that game already has a native PS4 release. Both are 2D games, of course, and the developer notes that plenty of other games are still sluggish. EmuFive doesn't run on top of the PS4's own operating system. It's a small Linux system, installed through PS4 Multiboot and started from a GoldHEN payload. 
At its core is KytyPS5, the same PS5 emulator that recently got Marvel's Wolverine to run on PC, and showed good progress in many other PS exclusive titles. Rather than emulating the PS5's processor, KytyPS5 hands the game's x86-64 code straight to the host CPU. That's an issue on the PS4, as its Jaguar cores lack the AVX2, FMA, and BMI2 extensions that Zen 2-targeted PS5 games use all over the place. Hammedi's patch gets around it by translating those instructions into older SSE4.2, AVX, and BMI1 equivalents, mostly at load time. That works, but it piles extra overhead onto a CPU that is already far slower.Games can be loaded from a USB drive, the PS4's internal storage, or a shared folder on a PC, though users have to bring their own game dumps, since none are included. Un equipo de investigadores de la Universidad Estatal de Carolina del Norte desarrolló un sistema que transforma el antebrazo en una superficie táctil capaz de controlar relojes inteligentes sin necesidad de tocar la pequeña pantalla del dispositivo. La tecnología, bautizada EpiPad, permite deslizar, hacer zoom y seleccionar opciones mediante gestos realizados directamente sobre la piel.
El sistema utiliza un sensor de radar de onda milimétrica (mmWave) de tamaño compacto para rastrear el movimiento de los dedos y medir con qué fuerza el usuario presiona la piel. Esta combinación habilita gestos con varios dedos y controles sensibles a la presión, de manera similar a lo que ofrece el panel táctil de una computadora portátil.

Today I learned the world's first mass-produced drone was built by a Hollywood actor
British-born actor Reginald Denny turned model aircraft into the Radioplane OQ-2
The first military drone built in serious numbers didn't come from a defense contractor or tech giant - but from Reginald Denny, a British-born silent film actor who sold model aircraft on Hollywood Boulevard.
His Radioplane OQ-2 was the first mass-produced drone in the United States - and by the end of World War II, his company had delivered nearly 15,000 target drones to the US Army according to the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum.
From film sets to model planes
Denny, whose real name was Reginald Leigh Dugmore, starred in nearly two hundred films over a half-century period, including both silent films and talkies. Apart from being a professional actor, he was also part of a Hollywood stunt pilot group called Thirteen Black Cats.
While he never saw aerial combat due to a training injury, Denny trained for the Royal Flying Corps in World War I as an observer and air gunner. His fascination for aircraft led him to open a hobby shop on Hollywood Boulevard in 1935, which he sold model airplanes and miniature engines.
In 1936, he developed his first radio-controlled prototype. The RP-1 had a nine-foot wingspan, ran on toy train motors, and used a simple rotary telephone dial to encode radio signals. He gave his first demonstration before the US Army in 1938.

articles.title: SGLang RCE Exploit Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data From 18 Agents and About 100 Users

An attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw in SGLang, an open-source inference engine, and ran code on one of NEAR AI's inference servers last Sunday.
The attacker could also have seen requests being processed on that server that day, including requests sent in confidential mode, the company said earlier this week. That mode processes requests inside a trusted execution environment (TEE) designed to keep them private even from the company itself.
But the TEE "does not protect against a vulnerability in the software running inside the environment," the company said. SGLang runs inside the TEE, which is how the attacker could reach requests there.
That access has since been closed, but not before the attacker moved further into the company's systems.
The attacker reached an internal system behind Private Chat, a product the company had already deprecated. So far, the company has confirmed that the attacker downloaded account details for about 100 users there. These are email addresses and names, and for some accounts, plan and balance information.
The company found no sign that stored Private Chat conversations or uploaded files were accessed.
The attacker also reached 18 AI agents on an older deployment of NEAR AI Agents that did not run inside the company's TEE. From those agents, the attacker took data including chat history, settings and logs.
Two customers' NEAR AI Cloud API keys were exposed in logs. The company has revoked both.

articles.title: Git Patches Flaw That Lets Malicious Repositories Execute Code During Recursive Clones
articles.summary:
A flaw in Git can let a malicious repository run an attacker's code on a computer that clones it recursively, together with its submodules. The Git project fixed it this week in Git 2.56.1, with matching fixes for the 2.50 through 2.55 series in 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1 and 2.55.1.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-111760, is an integer truncation in how Git handles its index. An extremely long path in a repository can pass Git's safety check, but Git then writes it to disk under a shorter name that an attacker can set to .git.
This lets an attacker replace a submodule's .git file with a symbolic link to a folder holding malicious hooks or configuration. Hooks are programs Git runs at set points, so once Git uses that folder, the attacker's code can run.
Submodules matter here because Git refuses to replace a .git folder with a symbolic link, but in a freshly cloned submodule, .git is a file.
The fixed versions, listed in the Git project's release announcement, refuse such extremely long paths before their length can be cut short.
GitHub, which ships Git in its own tools, explained the fixes in a detailed write-up. It advises installing a fixed version from your operating system or Git distributor, and updating any app that ships its own copy of Git.
The company has already applied the fixes to github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For GitHub Enterprise Server, they are in versions 3.19.15, 3.20.11, 3.21.9 and 3.22.4.

articles.title: Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
articles.summary:
An AI model can be given a hidden backdoor by editing fewer than 10 of its rarely used neurons, without retraining the model, Microsoft researchers have shown.
When a chosen trigger appears, the model outputs an attacker's command, which an agent using that model would run with the agent's own permissions. The attacker must be able to change the model's weights.
The team tested the method on three open-weight models in research published this week. Microsoft says it has not seen any threat actors use the technique. The company also published guidance on defending against it.
The edited neurons are ones that rarely fire and barely affect the model's answers. They were set to fire only when a trigger string appears, either in a user's request or later in a tool's output.
The researchers call the method Lazarus. Each edited neuron forces one token of the command into the model's output, so a command needs about one neuron per token.
The new neuron settings are calculated directly and can then be tuned with a few hundred training steps on those neurons alone. Nothing else in the model file or the code that runs it changes.
In a researcher's walkthrough posted on X, a backdoored Nemotron-Terminal-8B model with 10 edited neurons was tasked with fixing a Node.js server. It worked normally for three turns.
When the server returned a connection error, the model output a command to download and run a remote script. The script ran as root inside the test container and printed a banner n…

articles.summary:
AI provider keys that customers stored on Railway were stolen in an October breach and used to commit an estimated $740,000 in unauthorized spending, the platform-as-a-service provider said yesterday. It has promised to pay those charges itself when an AI provider will not refund them.
The company builds and runs apps for its customers and stores their secrets, such as API keys and database credentials, as environment variables. The attacker decrypted variables in at most 1.85% of workspaces, about 100,000, and its database queries looked for AI provider keys.
In an October 26 update, the company told customers asking about refunds for unauthorized AI spend that "Railway is unable to refund customers for spend performed with compromised API keys." It encouraged them to contact the AI providers directly and offered to escalate their requests.
According to the company's incident report, the decrypted data also included linked-account tokens for 1,852 users: BYOK agent keys and GitHub OAuth tokens. All were reset, each user was notified, and no logins to customer accounts using stolen credentials were found.
In addition to AI keys, one of the attacker's database queries matched cloud, database, and payment service credentials. The company's forensics did not show any customer databases being accessed, and there was no indication that customers' code repositories were downloaded.

articles.title: eMudhra Revokes 8 More CAs It Previously Declared Unaffected by Key Compromise
articles.summary:
The in-house Python script behind eMudhra's October key compromise has now cost the company 8 more of its intermediate certificate authorities (CAs), even though it did not weaken their keys.
Each intermediate CA has its own private key, which the company uses to sign the certificates it issues. The 8 intermediate CAs compromised in October had a different problem: a single line in the script cut each of their keys to one byte, the company said this week.
The script also retrieved the RSA keys of the 8 newly revoked CAs from the company's hardware security modules (HSMs). The company says it cannot show that the keys were handled as required by its own rules. It revoked the CAs late last week.
The company had called those CAs unaffected. "The RSA issuers went through a different path as per our assessment of the code and are therefore not impacted," it wrote on Mozilla's bug tracker on October 19.
Of the 8, 6 were for website (TLS) certificates and 2 for code signing. The company had put 4 of them into production in May. Its list names 195 certificates from them, 29 for its own domains.
Both problems began at a key ceremony on April 30, 2025, according to the full incident report the company posted to the same bug tracker this week. That day it generated 16 CA keys on Utimaco HSMs, including the 8 behind the October key compromise.
The keys were meant for Crypto4A HSMs at the company's US and EU sites. Moving keys between HSMs from different vendors is limited, the company sa…

articles.title: We Built An Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules. Here's What We Learned.
articles.summary:
We tell customers three things about securing AI agents: they need their own identities, access that fits the job they’re given, and traceability that’s separate from any human’s. That was true for us at Token as well. Then, we built an agent that broke all three by default.
This helped us think through how such agents should be defended. When a browser agent acts inside a user’s authenticated session, the application may see the user but not the agent, the delegation, or the task’s intended scope. By creating an agent that breaks all the security rules, Token learned how companies should be using identity to gain control, especially as agent use scales. Standards are coming, but there are steps security teams can take today.
The agent we would have flagged
The agent we created is named Rehearsal. Its job is to answer questions inside the Token platform by doing rather than telling. It autonomously opens pages in the browser tab, sets filters, and fills in forms.
From a security perspective, it’s a typical UI agent that runs in the user’s browser. That’s what makes it useful. But it also means the agent runs within the user’s session and has their reach.
Moreover, to the server behind the page, the agent’s clicks are inherently indistinguishable from the user’s, because nothing in a session cookie points to who the session driver is.

articles.title: Por qué tu móvil muestra ‘5G’ y el de otros ‘5G+’
articles.summary:
Algunos usuarios de iPhone notan, desde hace poco más de un mes, un cambio en la parte superior de la pantalla de su teléfono: junto a las barras de cobertura móvil aparece el ícono ‘5G+’ en lugar del habitual ‘5G’. El fenómeno no es aislado. Cada vez más usuarios reportan la misma novedad, que coincide con la actualización a iOS 27.
La explicación tiene que ver con una distinción técnica que existía desde hace años, pero que hasta ahora los teléfonos no mostraban: la diferencia entre la red 5G convencional y el 5G “real” o Stand Alone.
Hasta la llegada de este nuevo distintivo, todos los usuarios veían el mismo ícono de ‘5G’ en sus pantallas, sin posibilidad de saber si estaban conectados a una red 5G NSA, con arquitectura apoyada parcialmente en infraestructura 4G, o a una red 5G SA, diseñada de punta a punta para la nueva tecnología.

El ‘5G+’ es el nombre comercial que operadores como Orange y Movistar adoptaron, allá por 2023, para identificar la red 5G SA (Stand Alone) frente al 5G NSA que desplegaron inicialmente las compañías. La arquitectura Stand Alone implica que tanto la red de acceso radio como el núcleo central están construidos específicamente para 5G, sin depender de la infraestructura 4G previa.
